summary: Fan-out web research on training-free LLM/VLM model-cascade & deferral methods; return a structured, deduped, ranked catalog mapped to our checkpoint setup

methods.name: Chow's rule (optimal reject-option / Bayes abstention)
methods.paper: On Optimum Recognition Error and Reject Tradeoff (C.K. Chow), IEEE Transactions on Information Theory IT-16(1):41-46
methods.mechanism: Abstain/defer when the maximum posterior class probability max_y p(y|x) is below a threshold t; equivalently defer when the conditional expected risk exceeds the reject cost. Under known true posteriors this is the Bayes-optimal error-reject tradeoff. In a cascade it becomes: escalate to 32B when the 7B's top-1 probability < t.
methods.signal_required: Cheap-model top-1 class probability (the max of the per-class posterior).
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: YES. Our 7B cap320 per-letter logprob dict gives the full posterior, so max-prob = exp(max logprob) is directly computable per sample; threshold t (or our tau) is fixed on PMC-train using 7B's own correctness. This is essentially the canonical version of what we already do, only thresholding max-prob instead of top1-top2 margin.
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: NONE.
methods.expected_strength: Won't beat margin by much when classes are few and well-separated, but max-prob is the theoretically-grounded Bayes rule and can differ from margin when the top-2 gap is large yet absolute confidence is low (e.g. a flat-but-peaked distribution): it escalates on absolute uncertainty rather than relative top-2 separation, which can save compute on confidently-correct items margin would needlessly escalate.

methods.name: Maximum Softmax Probability (MSP / Softmax Response) baseline
methods.paper: A Baseline for Detecting Misclassified and Out-of-Distribution Examples in Neural Networks (Hendrycks & Gimpel), ICLR
methods.mechanism: Score each input by its maximum softmax probability; flag/defer the lowest-scoring (least confident) inputs by thresholding. Identical decision boundary to Chow's rule for a calibrated softmax. In our cascade: escalate when 7B max softmax prob < threshold.
methods.signal_required: Cheap-model full softmax (or just its maximum entry).
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: YES. Identical computation to Chow's rule on our 7B per-letter logprobs; softmax over the letter logprob dict, take the max, threshold on PMC-train. No 32B signal needed.
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: NONE.
methods.expected_strength: Same caveats as Chow; it is the standard strong baseline. It will rarely beat a well-tuned margin in our few-option MCQ setting, but is the reference point every cascade paper reports, so it belongs in the bake-off. Its known weakness (overconfidence) is exactly why margin/entropy/energy variants exist.

methods.name: Prediction margin (top1-top2 gap) — current method
methods.paper: Active Learning Literature Survey (B. Settles) formalizes margin sampling M(x)=p_top1 - p_top2; widely reused for selective prediction
methods.mechanism: Score = difference between the most-probable and second-most-probable class probabilities; defer when the margin is small. Escalate to 32B when 7B (top1 - top2) < tau. This is exactly our deployed gate (tau=0.426).
methods.signal_required: Cheap-model top-1 and top-2 class probabilities.
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: YES — this is our current gate, fully derivable from the 7B per-letter logprob dict; tau calibrated on PMC-train with 7B's own correctness.
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: NONE.
methods.expected_strength: It is the incumbent; the question is what beats IT. Margin is strong precisely when the relevant uncertainty is binary confusion between the top two options (common in 4-way MCQ). It can be beaten when uncertainty is spread across >2 options (entropy/Gini capture that) or when absolute confidence matters more than relative separation (max-prob/Chow).

methods.name: Predictive entropy / least-confidence (uncertainty-sampling triad)
methods.paper: Active Learning Literature Survey (B. Settles); entropy H(x)=-sum_y p_y log p_y, least-confidence C(x)=1-max_y p_y
methods.mechanism: Defer when the full-distribution Shannon entropy is high (or equivalently least-confidence 1-maxprob is high) beyond a threshold. Escalate to 32B when 7B answer-letter entropy > threshold. Entropy uses the whole posterior, not just top-1/top-2.
methods.signal_required: Cheap-model full class-probability distribution (all letters).
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: YES. Our 7B per-letter logprob dict is the full distribution over A/B/C/D(/E), so entropy and least-confidence are directly computable per sample; threshold fixed on PMC-train via 7B correctness. No 32B needed.
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: NONE.
methods.expected_strength: Beats margin on compute-saving-at-iso-accuracy when the 7B's mistakes are 3+-way confusions (mass diffused across several options) rather than clean top-2 ties: entropy escalates those and retains genuinely-peaked answers, whereas margin can be fooled by a low top1-top2 gap even when option 3+ carry mass. In medical MCQ with 4-5 plausible distractors this multi-way case is plausible.

methods.name: DOCTOR (Gini-impurity / quadratic-confidence detector, D_alpha)
methods.paper: DOCTOR: A Simple Method for Detecting Misclassification Errors (Granese, Romanelli, Gorla, Palamidessi, Piantanida), NeurIPS
methods.mechanism: Totally-Black-Box detector scores reliability via the quadratic sum g_hat(x)=sum_k p_k(x)^2; D_alpha defers when (1 - g_hat(x)) exceeds gamma*g_hat(x), i.e. thresholds Gini impurity 1-sum p_k^2. Penalizes diffuse (high-entropy) posteriors more aggressively than MSP near the simplex boundary.
methods.signal_required: Cheap-model full soft-prediction vector (all class probabilities).
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: YES (the TBB / D_alpha variant). Gini = 1 - sum over letters of p^2 is directly computable from the 7B per-letter logprob dict; gamma/threshold tuned on PMC-train with 7B correctness. The PBB variant (input-gradient preprocessing) is NOT implementable from saved checkpoints and we would skip it.
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: NONE for D_alpha (TBB). The gradient-based PBB variant would need a forward+backward GPU re-run (skip it).
methods.expected_strength: Like entropy, it uses the whole distribution, so it can beat margin when uncertainty is multi-way; the quadratic (Gini) form weights the top probabilities differently from log-entropy and was shown to edge out MSP/entropy/ODIN on misclassification detection in the original paper, so it is a cheap extra contender for the bake-off with a different operating curve.

methods.name: Energy score (logit energy as confidence)
methods.paper: Energy-based Out-of-distribution Detection (Liu, Wang, Owens, Li), NeurIPS
methods.mechanism: Score each input by the (free) energy E(x) = -T * logsumexp(f_y(x)/T) over class logits; lower energy = more confident/in-distribution. Defer when energy is high (less negative). In our cascade: escalate when 7B energy over its answer-letter logits exceeds a threshold. Parameter-free, post-hoc; theoretically aligned with input density and less prone to softmax overconfidence.
methods.signal_required: Cheap-model raw class logits (pre-softmax) over the candidate classes.
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: PARTIAL/YES-with-caveat. Our stored signal is per-letter LOGPROBS, not raw logits. logsumexp of logprobs = log(sum p) = log(1) approx 0 over a normalized full distribution, so energy is only well-defined if the stored values are unnormalized logits or restricted to the constrained answer-letter logit subset. If the dict holds the constrained-decoding logprobs (not full-vocab), energy degenerates; an exact energy score requires the raw answer-token logits. Derivable from checkpoints ONLY if the saved values are true logits.
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: If stored values are normalized logprobs (likely), a lightweight 7B re-run capturing raw answer-letter LOGITS (or full-vocab logits at the answer position) is needed; no sampling/decoding beyond the single answer token.
methods.expected_strength: Energy beats softmax-based scores (MSP/margin) most when overconfidence is the failure mode — the 7B is confidently wrong on out-of-its-competence images (e.g. PathVQA/hard cases). Energy's density-alignment can flag those for escalation that a saturated softmax margin would keep, improving iso-accuracy compute saving on distribution-shifted benchmarks.

methods.name: MaxLogit (maximum unnormalized logit)
methods.paper: Scaling Out-of-Distribution Detection for Real-World Settings (Hendrycks, Basart, Mazeika, et al.), ICML
methods.mechanism: Score by the single largest pre-softmax logit max_y f_y(x); defer when it is low. Avoids the softmax's normalization (which can hide low absolute evidence behind a sharp peak), so it separates confident-correct from low-evidence cases better at large scale.
methods.signal_required: Cheap-model raw logit vector (the maximum logit value).
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: PARTIAL. Same caveat as energy: needs raw logits, not normalized logprobs. If our dict stores constrained-decode logprobs, MaxLogit is not recoverable (max logprob is just log of max-prob, i.e. collapses to MSP up to monotone transform). Recoverable only if stored values are true logits.
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: If stored values are logprobs: a 7B re-run capturing raw answer-position logits (no extra decoding) to expose unnormalized max-logit.
methods.expected_strength: Beats MSP/margin chiefly in large-label-space, high-distribution-shift settings where softmax normalization erases absolute-evidence signal. In our 4-5-way MCQ the gain over MSP is typically small (the original paper found ~0.14% in small-label settings), so it is a low-priority contender unless the answer-letter logits prove informative.

methods.name: Temperature-scaled confidence (post-hoc calibration before thresholding)
methods.paper: On Calibration of Modern Neural Networks (Guo, Pleiss, Sun, Weinberger), ICML
methods.mechanism: Rescale logits z -> z/T by a single temperature T fit on a held-out set to minimize NLL/ECE, then apply any confidence rule (max-prob, margin, entropy) on the calibrated probabilities and threshold. Calibration sharpens the relationship between the confidence signal and true correctness so the deferral threshold is more reliable.
methods.signal_required: Cheap-model class logits (for the T/T rescale) and a calibration set with correctness labels to fit T.
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: YES (calibration-only). T is a one-parameter fit on PMC-train using the 7B's OWN correctness labels (which we have); then re-threshold margin/max-prob/entropy on T-scaled probs. Works exactly on our logprob dict (rescale logprobs by 1/T, renormalize). No 32B needed. Note: T is a monotone transform, so it can shift WHERE the threshold sits and improve cross-benchmark transfer, but on a single benchmark it cannot change the ranking of samples by max-prob (so it helps generalization/threshold-transfer, not within-set ordering).
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: NONE if logprobs suffice for the rescale; none for fitting T (uses existing PMC-train correctness).
methods.expected_strength: Wins on compute-saving-at-iso-accuracy when the 7B is mis-calibrated and the SAME tau must transfer across six benchmarks with different difficulty: temperature scaling aligns confidence-to-correctness so a single calibrated threshold escalates the right fraction per benchmark, reducing over-escalation on easy benchmarks and under-escalation on hard ones that a raw-margin tau (fit only on PMC) gets wrong. Directly targets our 63%-escalation over-deferral problem via better-calibrated thresholding.

methods.name: Confidence-based cascade deferral: theory of when it suffices (and post-hoc deferral when it doesn't)
methods.paper: When Does Confidence-Based Cascade Deferral Suffice? (Jitkrittum, Gupta, Menon, Narasimhan, Rawat, Kumar), NeurIPS
methods.mechanism: Characterizes the Bayes-optimal cascade deferral rule and shows simple cheap-model confidence (max-prob/Chow, margin) is near-optimal when downstream errors are 'nested' (large model right wherever it matters), but provably fails when the large model is a specialist, under label noise, or distribution shift. Proposes a post-hoc deferral rule that estimates the relative benefit of escalation (modelling the LARGE model's error), not just the small model's confidence.
methods.signal_required: For the confidence rules: cheap-model max-prob/margin (training-free). For the post-hoc improvement: cheap-model outputs AND large-model correctness labels on a held-out set to learn the deferral classifier.
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: PARTIAL. The diagnostic/confidence half is exactly our setting and confirms margin should be hard to beat — usable as the framing/justification. The post-hoc deferral improvement is NOT directly implementable: it needs 32B correctness on the SAME calibration distribution to model downstream errors, and our calibration set has only 7B-on-PMC-train correctness (no 32B-on-calib labels).
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: To build the post-hoc deferral classifier: re-run the 32B on PMC-train (and ideally per-benchmark held-out slices) to obtain strong-model correctness labels, then fit the deferral rule on (7B-signals, [7B-correct, 32B-correct]).
methods.expected_strength: This is the principled way to beat margin: instead of escalating on absolute 7B uncertainty, escalate only where the 32B is actually likely to FIX the answer (high estimated escalation benefit). On our four competent benchmarks where some 7B errors the 32B also misses (e.g. near-chance MedXpert-like items), it would stop wasting 32B compute on unrecoverable cases, cutting escalation rate below 63% at the same accuracy — the single biggest lever for our compute-saving goal.

methods.name: FrugalGPT LLM cascade (sequential confidence-gated escalation)
methods.paper: FrugalGPT: How to Use Large Language Models While Reducing Cost and Improving Performance (Chen, Zaharia, Zou), TMLR / arXiv
methods.mechanism: Query models cheapest-first; a learned generation-scoring function rates the cheap model's answer reliability, and if the score clears a per-stage threshold the answer is returned, else escalate to the next (more expensive) model. The router and per-stage thresholds are optimized to hit a cost budget.
methods.signal_required: A reliability score for the cheap model's GENERATED answer (their scorer is a small trained regressor on the answer text/features); not raw logprobs.
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: PARTIAL. The cascade structure is exactly ours (7B then 32B). But FrugalGPT's specific scorer is a TRAINED reliability regressor over generated text and requires labeled (query, answer, correctness) data to train; with logprobs available we'd typically substitute a logprob-confidence scorer (which then collapses to the Chow/margin/entropy methods above). The trained-scorer variant needs labels.
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: NONE for inference signals if we reuse 7B logprobs; but training the FrugalGPT-style scorer needs correctness labels — for a true 2-stage benefit estimate that means 32B labels on a calibration split (GPU re-run of 32B on PMC-train).
methods.expected_strength: Its advantage over a single margin threshold is the LEARNED scorer combining multiple features (and, in the full method, multi-model routing). For our 2-model case the realizable gain over margin comes only from a richer learned scorer on 7B features + downstream-benefit labels — i.e. it reduces to the Jitkrittum post-hoc deferral idea. As a pure training-free drop-in it does not beat margin; it is included as the canonical LLM-cascade reference.

methods.name: Chow-quantile / token-level uncertainty deferral for LM cascades
methods.paper: Language Model Cascades: Token-level Uncertainty and Beyond (Gupta, Jitkrittum, Menon, Narasimhan, Rawat, Kumar, et al.)
methods.mechanism: For generative cascades, the sequence softmax probability is length-biased (defers long answers regardless of quality). Instead, take QUANTILES of the per-token uncertainty vector as the deferral signal (Chow-Quantile), and optionally a learned rule combining several quantiles, to decide escalation to the large model.
methods.signal_required: Cheap-model PER-TOKEN logprobs across the whole generated answer sequence (a vector of token uncertainties), not a single class distribution.
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: NO / mostly N/A as stored. Our 7B cheap leg decodes only a SINGLE answer letter (constrained), so there is no multi-token sequence to take quantiles over — the length-bias problem this method solves does not arise for us, and the method has no signal to act on. It would only become relevant if we switched the 7B cheap leg to free-form (multi-token) answering.
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: Would require re-running the 7B in free-form generation mode to emit a multi-token answer with per-token logprobs; otherwise inapplicable.
methods.expected_strength: Beats simple confidence only in the generative/long-output regime where length bias corrupts sequence-prob deferral. Since our cheap leg emits one letter, this offers no compute-saving edge for the current design; documented here to justify EXCLUDING it (its core premise — token-level/length effects — does not apply to single-letter MCQ decoding).

families.family_summary: The classic selective-prediction / confidence-cascade family traces to Chow's 1970 optimal reject-option rule (defer when the top posterior is below a threshold) and its modern incarnations: the Maximum-Softmax-Probability baseline (Hendrycks & Gimpel 2017), softmax response (Geifman & El-Yaniv 2017), and the uncertainty-sampling triad of least-confidence / margin (top1-top2) / predictive entropy (Settles 2009) — all training-free, post-hoc scores thresholded on a calibration set. Distribution-aware refinements add Gini-impurity (DOCTOR, 2021), and logit-space scores that resist softmax overconfidence: energy (Liu et al. 2020) and MaxLogit (Hendrycks et al. 2022); temperature scaling (Guo et al. 2017) calibrates any of these before thresholding so a single threshold transfers across datasets. The modern theory of cascades (Jitkrittum et al. NeurIPS 2023; Gupta et al. 2024; FrugalGPT 2023) establishes that simple cheap-model confidence (Chow/margin) is remarkably hard to beat when downstream errors are nested, but provably fails under specialists/label-noise/shift — where a learned POST-HOC deferral rule that estimates the strong model's benefit (not just the weak model's uncertainty) wins. For OUR checkpoints, every full-distribution score (Chow/MSP, margin, entropy, least-confidence, Gini/DOCTOR-TBB, plus temperature-scaled variants) is computable today from the 7B per-letter logprob dict with PMC-train calibration and NO GPU re-run; logit-space scores (energy, MaxLogit) need raw answer-token logits if our stored values are normalized logprobs; and the genuinely-better learned/post-hoc deferral (Jitkrittum-style) — the most promising route to push escalation below 63% at parity — requires a one-time 32B re-run on the calibration split to obtain strong-model correctness labels, while the token-level Chow-quantile line is inapplicable because our cheap leg decodes only a single answer letter.

The LLM-cascade family runs a cheap model first and escalates to an expensive model only when a per-sample deferral/scoring function fires; the variation across the family is entirely in (a) what signal the scoring function reads and (b) whether that function is trained, calibrated, or fully training-free. The cleanest mapping to our setup is the "token-level uncertainty" line of Language Model Cascades (Chow-Sum / Chow-Average / Chow-Quantile, NeurIPS 2024 / arXiv 2404.10136): these are fully training-free, read only the cheap model's per-token logprobs, and the headline finding is that QUANTILES of the per-token distribution (esp. low quantiles = worst-token confidence) carry richer, complementary uncertainty than a single sequence-probability or the top1-top2 margin — directly implementable on our 7B per-letter logprob dict and the most likely thing to beat our current margin gate at iso-accuracy. The other dominant signal families are self-consistency/agreement (Mixture of Thoughts ICLR'24, Agreement-Based Cascading, SMART) which need MULTIPLE cheap samples (a GPU re-run at temperature>0 on our greedy-only checkpoints), and self-verification (AutoMix) which needs an extra generation pass where the cheap model judges its own answer. FrugalGPT and the Unified Routing+Cascading framework both rely on a separately TRAINED scorer/quality-estimator (DistilBERT or small classifiers) plus a calibration-set threshold/grid search, so only their calibration-side machinery (cost-aware threshold selection under a budget) is training-free and reusable; the scorer itself is not. Cascade-Aware Training retrains the small model and so is out of scope for a training-free deliverable. For our exact constraints — single greedy decode, 7B full per-letter softmax, 32B logprob-free, calibration with 7B's own correctness only — the immediately implementable, no-rerun winners are the Chow-Quantile/entropy/energy/topk-gap variants on the existing 7B logprob dict, with the multi-sample consistency methods being the strongest candidates IF a temperature-sampling GPU re-run is permitted.

methods.name: Chow-Quantile deferral (token-level uncertainty cascade)
methods.paper: Language Model Cascades: Token-level uncertainty and beyond (Jitkrittum et al.)
methods.mechanism: Aggregate the cheap model's per-token log-probabilities into a single deferral score, but instead of summing (Chow-Sum) or length-normalizing (Chow-Average), take a QUANTILE of the per-token confidence (e.g. the min / 0-quantile = worst token, or a low quantile). Defer to the strong model when the score falls below a threshold tau. Different quantiles capture complementary uncertainty; the paper shows quantile aggregation beats sum/average.
methods.signal_required: Cheap model's per-token log-probabilities of its greedy-decoded answer (no full softmax strictly needed; top-1 chosen-token logprob per position suffices). Single greedy decode only.
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: PARTIAL→YES. Our 7B answer is effectively a SINGLE answer-letter token, so 'per-token quantiles over a sequence' degenerates. BUT the same paper's core insight transfers directly to our one-token full softmax: we already have the full per-letter logprob dict, so we can compute quantiles/order-statistics OVER THE LETTER DISTRIBUTION (top1, top2, ... gaps), plus min-letter-prob, entropy, energy. Fully derivable offline from saved checkpoints; no rerun. For the multi-token spirit we'd need a generated-sequence trace (see needs_gpu_rerun).
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: NONE for the single-letter-distribution version (entropy/quantile-over-letters/topk-gaps from existing logprob dict). To get the true multi-token per-position quantiles you'd need a 7B re-run that decodes a short answer span and stores per-position logprobs (we currently store only the letter).
methods.expected_strength: Beats a top1-top2 margin when the discriminating information lives in the SHAPE of the distribution rather than just the top-2 gap — e.g. a flat tail (high entropy) or a strong third option signals difficulty that an equal top-2 gap misses. Entropy/energy over the full letter softmax is a strictly richer scalar than margin at zero extra compute, so it can shift the cost-accuracy frontier and lower escalation rate at the same accuracy.

methods.name: Chow-Sum / Chow-Average (sequence log-prob & length-normalized perplexity gate)
methods.paper: Language Model Cascades: Token-level uncertainty and beyond (Jitkrittum et al.)
methods.mechanism: Deferral score = total log-prob of the cheap model's generated answer (Chow-Sum) or its length-normalized version / negative log-perplexity (Chow-Average). Defer when below tau. These are the classic confidence baselines the paper shows are biased (Sum favors long, Average over-corrects).
methods.signal_required: Cheap model's logprobs of the generated answer sequence; single greedy decode. For a one-token answer this reduces to the chosen-letter logprob (max-prob confidence).
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: YES. For our single-letter answer, Chow-Average ≈ the chosen-letter probability (max-prob confidence), which is directly in the 7B per-letter logprob dict. Computable offline, no rerun. Serves as a baseline alongside margin.
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: NONE (chosen-letter logprob already saved).
methods.expected_strength: Rarely beats margin on its own for single-token MCQ (max-prob and margin are highly correlated), but it is the canonical baseline and is essentially free. Useful mainly as a frontier reference and as a feature to combine with margin/entropy; unlikely to be the standalone winner.

methods.name: Post-Hoc-Quantile / Post-Hoc-Embed deferral classifier
methods.paper: Language Model Cascades: Token-level uncertainty and beyond (Jitkrittum et al.)
methods.mechanism: Train a small feedforward deferral classifier on top of the quantile features (Post-Hoc-Quantile) and optionally intermediate decoder embeddings of both models (Post-Hoc-Embed-1+2) to predict whether deferring helps. This was the paper's best-performing variant.
methods.signal_required: Quantile features of cheap-model token logprobs, plus (for the embed variant) hidden-state embeddings from cheap and/or strong model. Requires labels indicating beneficial deferral cases.
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: NO (as the deployed best variant). It needs (a) labels of 'deferral helps' which require 32B-on-calibration labels we DON'T have (calibration is 7B-on-PMC-train with 7B's own correctness only), and the embed variant needs strong-model hidden states (32B is logprob/hidden-free here). A degraded quantile-only classifier trained on 7B-own-correctness is possible but contradicts a training-free deliverable and lacks the strong-model label.
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: 32B-on-PMC-train labels (to define the deferral target), and for the embed variant, hidden-state extraction from 7B and 32B on calibration.
methods.expected_strength: Would beat margin most when a single hand-picked quantile/threshold is suboptimal across the 4 heterogeneous benchmarks (the paper notes no single quantile wins everywhere), letting a learned combine adapt. But it crosses out of 'training-free' and needs strong-model labels we lack, so it is a stretch for this project.

methods.name: FrugalGPT LLM cascade (DistilBERT generation scorer + budget-optimized thresholds)
methods.paper: FrugalGPT: How to Use Large Language Models While Reducing Cost and Improving Performance (Chen, Zaharia, Zou)
methods.mechanism: A trained generation scoring function g(query, answer)→[0,1] (a DistilBERT regressor over the concatenated question+generated answer TEXT) estimates reliability of each model's output; if g>threshold accept, else escalate to the next, more expensive model. Cascade order and per-stage thresholds are jointly optimized on a validation set (grid/constrained search) under a cost budget.
methods.signal_required: The generated ANSWER TEXT of each model (not logprobs) fed to a separately trained scorer; plus a labeled validation set to fit g and the thresholds.
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: PARTIAL. The cascade STRUCTURE and the budget-constrained threshold-selection are reusable training-free (we already do a calibrated tau). The deployed scorer g is a TRAINED DistilBERT needing answer-correctness labels — trainable on our 7B-on-PMC-train correctness (we have raw_output text), but for single-letter MCQ a text scorer adds little over the logprobs we already have, and it is not training-free.
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: NONE for inputs (raw_output text already saved); but fitting g requires a (small) training step on calibration labels (CPU). Not a GPU rerun.
methods.expected_strength: Beats margin when the failure mode is detectable from answer TEXT/format but invisible in logprobs (e.g. hedging, malformed answers, refusals) — less relevant for single-letter MCQ where margin already captures the decision. Its real reusable contribution is the cost-budget joint threshold optimization, not the scorer.

methods.name: Mixture of Thought (MoT) consistency cascade
methods.paper: Large Language Model Cascades with Mixture of Thought Representations for Cost-Efficient Reasoning (Yue et al., ICLR 2024)
methods.mechanism: Sample MULTIPLE answers from the cheap model and use answer CONSISTENCY as the difficulty signal: (1) Voting — sample k answers (temperature/prompt variation), measure agreement; (2) Verification — compare the most-consistent answers across two thought representations (Chain-of-Thought vs Program-of-Thought); accept the cheap answer if consistent enough, else escalate. A single consistency threshold aligns agreement with the cost budget (tuned on validation, no trained classifier).
methods.signal_required: Multiple sampled cheap-model outputs (k>1) under temperature and/or two prompt/thought styles. Needs generated answers, not logprobs.
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: NO on current checkpoints (we have a SINGLE greedy decode and no-think only). The consistency signal cannot be computed from one sample. It is calibration-only (threshold on a val set, no classifier), so it WOULD become implementable after a sampling re-run.
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: 7B temperature sampling (k samples per question, e.g. k=5) on eval + PMC-train; ideally also a 7B think/PoT pass to get a second thought representation for the verification variant.
methods.expected_strength: Self-consistency is among the strongest training-free difficulty signals in the literature and routinely beats single-pass softmax confidence on reasoning tasks; it would likely cut escalation at iso-accuracy more than margin, especially where the 7B is confidently wrong (low margin-error correlation) but inconsistent across samples. Cost: k cheap forward passes, which must be netted against compute saved.

methods.name: AutoMix (few-shot self-verification + POMDP/threshold meta-verifier)
methods.paper: AutoMix: Automatically Mixing Language Models (Madaan et al.)
methods.mechanism: After the cheap model answers, it self-VERIFIES via a few-shot prompt framed as an entailment/correctness check, producing a noisy reliability estimate; a meta-verifier (simple threshold or a POMDP that models verification noise and categorizes Simple/Complex/Unsolvable) maps that estimate to accept/escalate. Works with closed APIs, no weight access.
methods.signal_required: An extra cheap-model generation pass (the self-verification output / its yes-no probability). Optionally a few labeled examples to fit the POMDP/threshold. No strong-model signal, no hidden states.
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: PARTIAL→NO without a rerun. The self-verification pass is not in our checkpoints (we only stored the answer letter + its logprobs). The threshold/POMDP calibration is doable on our PMC-train correctness. So it is calibration-only but needs the extra verification generation.
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: 7B self-verification generation pass per question (one extra short forward/decode with the entailment-style prompt) on eval + calibration; cheaper than full k-sample self-consistency.
methods.expected_strength: Beats margin when the model's INTROSPECTIVE judgement of its own answer is better calibrated than its raw answer softmax — verification can catch confident-but-wrong cases that a margin threshold passes through. The POMDP meta-verifier specifically denoises a weak signal, which can stabilize the frontier vs a single hard threshold. Cost is one extra short pass, much less than k-sample consistency.

methods.name: Agreement-Based Cascading (ABC)
methods.paper: Agreement-Based Cascading for Efficient Inference (Narasimhan et al.)
methods.mechanism: At each cascade level use an ENSEMBLE of cheap models (or multiple cheap runs) and measure their AGREEMENT; high agreement = confident → accept, disagreement → defer to the larger level. Agreement among an ensemble is shown to be a stronger deferral signal than single-model softmax confidence (with supporting theory).
methods.signal_required: Multiple cheap predictions per query (an ensemble of distinct cheap models, or multiple stochastic runs). Agreement count/vote. No strong-model signal.
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: NO on current checkpoints (we have ONE model, ONE greedy decode → nothing to agree with). Becomes feasible only with either multiple cheap models or temperature sampling. Threshold is calibration-only once samples exist.
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: Either run an additional cheap model variant (e.g. 7B at a different resolution cap as a second ensemble member — we already have cap80/160/320/640 checkpoints, so cross-cap AGREEMENT is computable offline!) or temperature-sample the 7B. The cross-cap agreement angle needs no NEW rerun.
methods.expected_strength: Beats single-model margin because agreement aggregates independent error signals: two cheap views that disagree flag difficulty even when each individually looks confident. Notably, our EXISTING cap80/160/320/640 7B checkpoints form a ready-made cheap ensemble — agreement across resolution caps is a training-free, zero-rerun signal worth testing as a margin alternative.

methods.name: SMART (scale-down with accuracy guarantee via output-equivalence profiling)
methods.paper: SMART: Automatically Scaling Down Language Models with Accuracy Guarantees for Reduced Processing Fees
methods.mechanism: Profile cheaper models on a calibration set against the strongest model's outputs; pick the cheapest model whose probability of DEVIATING from the strong model's answer is below a user-set tolerance, giving a statistical accuracy guarantee. Per-query escalation uses a consistency/agreement signal sampled from the candidate cheap model to decide if it can be trusted within tolerance.
methods.signal_required: A calibration set with STRONG-MODEL outputs as the reference (to measure deviation probability) plus a per-query consistency/sampling signal from the cheap model.
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: NO. Its guarantee is defined relative to the strong model's outputs ON CALIBRATION, which we lack (no 32B-on-PMC-train labels; calibration is 7B-own-correctness only). Also uses a sampling/consistency signal we don't have (single greedy). Calibration-only in spirit, but needs strong-model calibration labels + cheap sampling.
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: 32B-on-PMC-train labels (to define output-equivalence target) AND 7B temperature sampling on calibration for the per-query consistency signal.
methods.expected_strength: Its distinctive win is a FORMAL accuracy-tolerance guarantee relative to always-32B (exactly our parity goal), letting you push escalation as low as the tolerance allows rather than at a hand-set margin tau. Would beat margin when you want a provable 'no worse than 32B by epsilon' budget knob; cost is strong-model calibration labels we currently lack.

methods.name: Unified Routing+Cascading (cost-aware optimal deferral threshold)
methods.paper: A Unified Approach to Routing and Cascading for LLMs (Dekoninck et al., ICML 2025)
methods.mechanism: Generalizes routing and cascading: at each step compute a cost-quality objective tau_i(x,lambda)=qhat_i(x) - lambda*chat_i(x) using ex-ante and POST-HOC quality estimates; continue/stop is the analytically OPTIMAL rule, and the budget multiplier lambda (and a stopping gamma) are derived to exactly meet a cost budget rather than grid-searched. Proven optimal under the estimator quality.
methods.signal_required: Per-model quality estimate qhat (post-hoc = after cheap generation) and cost estimate; the quality estimator can be a small trained classifier or, in principle, model confidence. Plus a validation set to set lambda/gamma.
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: PARTIAL. The OPTIMAL cost-budgeted threshold derivation is directly reusable training-free on TOP of any confidence signal we already have (margin/entropy) — it replaces our hand-tuned tau with a budget-derived, provably-optimal tau on the calibration set. The full method's learned quality estimators (small classifiers / strong-model quality) are not training-free and need strong-model labels we lack.
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: NONE if applied as 'optimal threshold on our existing 7B confidence + measured FLOPs costs' using 7B-own-correctness on calibration. The richer learned-estimator version would need 32B-on-PMC-train quality labels.
methods.expected_strength: Does not invent a new signal but EXTRACTS more from whatever signal we use: given a target compute budget it picks the deferral threshold that maximizes expected accuracy optimally, instead of our ad-hoc tau=0.426. This alone can move the operating point along the frontier for free; biggest gain when our current tau is mis-placed relative to the true cost-accuracy tradeoff at the 0.572-parity budget.

methods.name: Cascade-Aware Training (CAT)
methods.paper: Cascade-Aware Training of Language Models (Wang et al.)
methods.mechanism: Keep a standard confidence-threshold deferral (normalized neg-log-likelihood of the cheap model's sequence > tau → defer), but RETRAIN the small model with a cascade-aware loss (token-level masking that down-weights tokens unlearnable by the small model) so its confidence becomes a more reliable deferral indicator.
methods.signal_required: Cheap model's own sequence log-likelihood at inference (same as Chow-Average). The benefit comes from retraining the small model, not a new inference signal.
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: NO. The deferral signal is computable from our 7B logprobs, but the entire benefit requires FINE-TUNING the 7B with the cascade-aware objective, which is out of scope for a training-free deliverable and would change our frozen checkpoint.
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: Full 7B fine-tuning with the cascade-aware loss (a training run, not just inference), then re-decoding eval/calibration with the retrained model.
methods.expected_strength: Would beat a margin threshold on an off-the-shelf 7B because the retrained model's confidence is explicitly shaped to separate defer-vs-keep cases; the paper shows the same threshold rule works better after CAT. But it violates training-free and modifies the deployed model, so it is a documented contrast/upper-bound rather than a usable method here.

methods.name: AutoMix (Threshold variant)
methods.paper: AutoMix: Automatically Mixing Language Models (NeurIPS 2024)
methods.mechanism: The small model generates an answer, then the SAME small model is re-prompted with a few-shot 'is this answer Correct/Incorrect given the context?' prompt; the verifier probability v = P(correct) is read (optionally averaged over k>1 higher-temperature samples). Escalate to the large model when v < threshold t.
methods.signal_required: A self-verification probability from a SECOND forward pass: cheap model re-prompted to judge its own generated answer, reading P(Correct). Few-shot exemplars in the verifier prompt. Optionally k samples to average.
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: PARTIAL. The threshold variant is training-free and conceptually fits (cheap-model self-judgement, single threshold). BUT it needs a SECOND generative forward pass on the 7B (the verify prompt over the generated answer) which we do not have on disk — our 7B checkpoints store only a one-shot per-letter logprob dict for the answer, not a self-verification pass. Cannot be derived from saved logprobs.
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: 7B re-run: for each eval sample, feed back the 7B's chosen answer in a few-shot 'Correct/Incorrect given context+image' verify prompt and read P(Correct) (one extra forward pass per sample; k>1 if averaging). Note AutoMix assumes a textual CONTEXT passage to verify against; our med-VQA has an image not a passage, so the verify prompt must be adapted to image-grounded verification.
methods.expected_strength: Beats a raw margin threshold when the model's self-assessment of its own answer carries error signal that the top1-top2 letter gap does not — e.g. a sample where the 7B is internally torn between distractors yet emits a confident-looking margin. The explicit 'did I get this right?' framing can separate confidently-wrong from confidently-right cases the margin conflates, lowering escalation rate at iso-accuracy. Weak/no gain if our 7B's self-verification is as miscalibrated/redundant as its margin (likely for a small med model).

methods.name: AutoMix (POMDP meta-verifier / AutoMix3)
methods.paper: AutoMix: Automatically Mixing Language Models (NeurIPS 2024)
methods.mechanism: Same few-shot self-verification probability, but routing is a POMDP over latent query difficulty (Simple/Complex/Unsolvable). Verifier probabilities are discretized into observation bins (k=8 samples); a meta-verifier learns observation+reward functions from validation data and the policy decides trust-SLM vs invoke-LLM. AutoMix3 extends to a middle model, conditioning on SLM and MLM verifier probabilities.
methods.signal_required: Same self-verification probability as threshold variant, but binned over k=8 verification samples per question, PLUS a validation set with ground-truth correctness to fit the POMDP observation/reward model.
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: NO as-is. The POMDP fits observation/reward params on validation data (light calibration, not weight training), so it is 'calibration-only' in spirit, but it still requires (a) the k=8 self-verification samples per question (a GPU re-run we lack) and (b) a calibration set tying verifier observations to correctness. Our calibration (7B-on-PMC-train with own correctness) could supply the labels, but the verification observations themselves do not exist on disk.
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: 7B re-run to produce k=8 self-verification samples per eval AND per PMC-train calibration question; then fit the POMDP (CPU). Two-leg cascade only needs the 2-state version; AutoMix3 is irrelevant unless we add a third model.
methods.expected_strength: Wins over margin threshold when the self-verifier is NOISY but still informative: the POMDP denoises a noisy verification signal via its difficulty prior, capturing 'unsolvable' questions where escalation is wasted (32B also fails) and NOT escalating them — directly cutting compute at iso-accuracy in a way a monotone margin threshold cannot. Most valuable on our two excluded near-chance benchmarks; less so on the four competent ones.

methods.name: P(True) self-evaluation
methods.paper: Language Models (Mostly) Know What They Know (Kadavath et al., Anthropic 2022)
methods.mechanism: Model proposes an answer, then is re-prompted to evaluate whether that answer is True/False; the probability mass on the 'True' token is P(True), used as a confidence score. Calibration improves further when the model is shown many of its own sampled candidate answers before judging one. Deferral = escalate when P(True) < threshold.
methods.signal_required: A second forward pass: re-prompt the cheap model with its own proposed answer and read P('True'). Stronger variant feeds multiple sampled answers as context (needs sampling).
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: PARTIAL. P(True) is zero/few-shot (training-free), unlike the paper's separate trained P(IK) head which is NOT training-free. The paper's other key finding — large models are well-calibrated DIRECTLY on multiple-choice answer-token probabilities — IS already covered by our 7B per-letter logprobs (our margin/maxprob gate is essentially that). The distinct P(True) signal needs a second self-eval pass we do not have on disk.
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: 7B re-run: one extra forward pass per eval sample appending the chosen answer and reading P(True) token prob. The multi-sample variant additionally needs temperature sampling of several candidate answers first.
methods.expected_strength: Beats margin when the True/False self-judgement decorrelates errors from the first-pass letter distribution — the second pass re-reads the question+answer jointly and can catch first-pass overconfidence. On multiple-choice, however, the paper shows direct answer-prob calibration is already strong, so the marginal gain over our existing maxprob/margin gate may be small unless our 7B is systematically overconfident in its single greedy decode.

methods.name: Verbalized confidence (Just Ask for Calibration)
methods.paper: Just Ask for Calibration: Strategies for Eliciting Calibrated Confidence Scores from LMs Fine-Tuned with Human Feedback (Tian et al., EMNLP 2023)
methods.mechanism: Directly prompt the model to emit a confidence number (e.g. 'Confidence: 0-100%') alongside or after its answer; optionally elicit top-k answers each with a verbalized probability. Use the verbalized score as the deferral signal: escalate when verbalized confidence < threshold.
methods.signal_required: Generated text: the cheap model must VERBALIZE a confidence number (a decode of confidence tokens), not just answer logprobs.
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: NO on disk. Training-free, but our 7B checkpoints contain only the single-letter answer logprob dict and no verbalized-confidence generation. The paper's headline result (verbalized > conditional probs) was on RLHF chat models like GPT-4/Claude; our 7B MedVLThinker is a small RL-tuned med model whose verbalized confidence is likely poorly calibrated/overconfident (corroborated by VLM verbalized-confidence studies), so this is the weakest fit of the family.
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: 7B re-run with a prompt that asks for an explicit confidence value (extra generation tokens) per eval and per calibration question.
methods.expected_strength: Could beat margin only if the 7B's verbalized number is better-calibrated than its letter-margin — which the literature says is true for large RLHF models but typically FALSE for small/VLM models (verbalized confidence over-estimates). For our setup, low expected upside; mainly worth a cheap pilot to rule out, not a primary bet.

methods.name: Self-consistency as confidence (Mixture-of-Thoughts cascade)
methods.paper: Large Language Model Cascades with Mixture of Thoughts Representations for Cost-efficient Reasoning (Yue et al., ICLR 2024)
methods.mechanism: Sample several reasoning chains from the cheap model (CoT, and a mixture of CoT + Program-of-Thought); measure answer consistency (vote agreement) across samples as a difficulty signal; escalate to the strong model when consistency is below a threshold.
methods.signal_required: MULTIPLE stochastic samples from the cheap model (temperature sampling), then an agreement/vote-consistency score over the sampled answers. No logprobs needed; no trained scorer.
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: NO on disk. Fully training-free, but it fundamentally needs MULTIPLE samples per question, whereas we ran only a single greedy decode. The consistency signal cannot be reconstructed from one sample or from the per-letter logprob dict (logprobs approximate but are not the same as empirical multi-sample agreement, which is the paper's actual signal).
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: 7B re-run with temperature sampling (e.g. 5-10 samples per question) on both eval and PMC-train calibration; if using the think-CoT variant, also need 7B-think traces (we have only no-think single decode for the cheap leg).
methods.expected_strength: Strong candidate to beat margin: empirical multi-sample agreement captures epistemic uncertainty that a single-decode top1-top2 gap misses, and med-VQA studies report sample-consistency has the best DISCRIMINATION (ROC-AUC) among cheap proxies. Lowers escalation at iso-accuracy when many 'low-margin' questions are actually answered consistently across samples (margin under-confident). Main cost: it multiplies the cheap-leg compute by the sample count, which eats into the FLOPs saving — net win only if the consistency signal lets us escalate far fewer questions than the extra samples cost.

methods.name: Cascaded Selective Evaluation / Simulated Annotators (Trust or Escalate)
methods.paper: Trust or Escalate: LLM Judges with Provable Guarantees for Human Agreement (Jung et al., ICLR 2025)
methods.mechanism: Confidence = max-likelihood label under an ENSEMBLE of 'simulated annotators' (N few-shot in-context prompts with different exemplars per annotator, predictions averaged). Use a cheap judge first; if its confidence c < calibrated threshold lambda, escalate to a stronger judge. Thresholds are set by fixed-sequence hypothesis testing on a calibration set to give a provable agreement guarantee (1-alpha).
methods.signal_required: N few-shot forward passes (one per simulated annotator) of the cheap model, reading the predicted-label probability each time and averaging; PLUS a calibration set to set the risk-controlled threshold.
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: PARTIAL. Training-free (calibration-only, no weight updates) and its threshold-calibration step maps cleanly onto our PMC-train-with-own-correctness calibration. BUT the Simulated-Annotators confidence needs N distinct few-shot prompts re-run per question (we have only one greedy decode, no few-shot ensembling) so the core signal is missing on disk. The conformal/risk-control thresholding idea is portable to our existing margin signal even without re-running.
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: 7B re-run: N few-shot in-context passes per question (different exemplars) on eval AND calibration to build the ensemble confidence. If only borrowing the risk-controlled threshold-calibration (not the ensemble), NONE — it can wrap our current margin signal.
methods.expected_strength: The ensemble-of-perspectives confidence reduces variance versus a single greedy margin, so it discriminates better at the decision boundary and can hold accuracy while escalating fewer questions. Its distinctive edge is the PROVABLE risk-controlled threshold: instead of hand-tuning tau, it sets the smallest threshold meeting a target accuracy guarantee, which can find a less conservative operating point than our hand-frozen tau=0.426 and thus cut escalation/compute at the same accuracy floor.

methods.name: FrugalGPT (learned scoring-function cascade)
methods.paper: FrugalGPT: How to Use Large Language Models While Reducing Cost and Improving Performance (Chen, Zaharia, Zou, 2023)
methods.mechanism: A separate small scoring model g(query, answer) (DistilBERT regressor) assigns a 0-1 reliability score to the cheap model's answer; escalate to the next model in the cascade when the score is below a learned threshold. Both the scorer and the cascade order/thresholds are optimized on training data.
methods.signal_required: The cheap model's generated answer text fed to a SEPARATELY TRAINED verifier (DistilBERT) that outputs a reliability score.
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: NO. Explicitly NOT training-free: it trains a DistilBERT scorer and optimizes thresholds on labeled data. Included as the supervised-verifier contrast point for this family (shows the boundary of 'training-free'). Could in principle be trained using our 7B-on-PMC-train answers + correctness labels, but that violates the training-free constraint.
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: No new GPU inference for the signal (uses generated answers we could collect), but it requires TRAINING a scorer on labeled (answer, correct?) pairs — outside the training-free scope; and our scorer would only have PMC-train labels, not 32B-on-calibration labels.
methods.expected_strength: A learned text scorer can exploit answer/question content features invisible to a pure logprob margin (e.g. answer phrasing patterns correlated with errors), so at iso-accuracy it can escalate fewer questions than a margin threshold. But it needs labeled training data and a held-out scorer, so it is out of scope here and offered only as the upper-bound/contrast for what self-verification gives you for free.

families.family_summary: The self-verification / meta-verifier family decides escalation by asking the cheap model (or a cheap judge) to assess its own answer, rather than reading a single first-pass logprob margin. The canonical, training-free members are AutoMix (few-shot 'is my answer correct?' self-verification giving P(correct), thresholded — with an optional calibration-only POMDP meta-verifier to denoise it), P(True) self-evaluation (re-prompt for True/False on the proposed answer), verbalized confidence (ask the model to state a confidence number), self-consistency-as-confidence (multi-sample answer agreement, as in the Mixture-of-Thoughts cascade), and Cascaded Selective Evaluation / Simulated Annotators (an ensemble of few-shot perspectives with a risk-controlled, provably-calibrated escalation threshold); FrugalGPT is the closely related but explicitly trained-verifier contrast point. The shared limitation for OUR setup is decisive: every distinctive signal in this family requires at least one EXTRA forward pass on the 7B (a self-verification/True-False/verbalized pass) or MULTIPLE stochastic samples, none of which exist in our checkpoints — we stored only a single greedy decode with a per-letter answer-logprob dict, so the family is at best PARTIAL/NO implementable without a GPU re-run of the 7B, and the 32B's empty logprobs are irrelevant since the signals all come from the cheap leg. Of the family, self-consistency (best empirical discrimination on med-VQA, but multiplies cheap-leg compute) and AutoMix-threshold / Trust-or-Escalate's risk-controlled thresholding (which could replace our hand-frozen tau=0.426 with a guarantee-driven, less-conservative operating point) are the most promising to beat a plain margin at iso-accuracy; verbalized confidence is the weakest because small/VLM models are documented to verbalize overconfidently. The one piece usable WITHOUT any re-run is the conformal/risk-controlled threshold-calibration idea from Trust or Escalate, which can wrap our existing margin signal to pick tau under a provable accuracy floor.

methods.name: CP-Router (Conformal-Prediction Router between LLM and LRM)
methods.paper: CP-Router: An Uncertainty-Aware Router Between LLM and LRM (AAAI 2026; arXiv 2505.19970)
methods.mechanism: Build a split-conformal prediction set C(x) over the MCQA answer letters from the cheap model's softmax, using nonconformity score S(x,y)=1-f(y) and a calibration quantile at level alpha. Route to the cheap model (LLM) if |C(x)| <= tau (typically tau=1, i.e. a singleton set), escalate to the strong model (LRM) if |C(x)| > 1. A 'Full and Binary Entropy' (FBE) criterion picks a single global alpha* that maximizes separation of set-size distributions, replacing a hand-tuned alpha.
methods.signal_required: Cheap-model full per-option softmax/logprobs over the answer letters (single greedy decode of the letter). No strong-model signal at inference. This is essentially our 7B per-letter logprob dict.
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: YES. Our 7B cap320 emits the full per-letter logprob dict, so softmax over A/B/C/D... gives the exact nonconformity score 1-f(y) and the prediction set. The conformal quantile is computed from 7B-on-PMC-train with its OWN correctness labels (marginal coverage only needs (x, y_true) + cheap softmax), which is exactly our calibration data. The 32B's empty logprobs are irrelevant since CP-Router never needs strong-model confidence. FBE is computable from set-size distributions on our eval/calib softmax. This is the single most directly droppable method onto our checkpoints.
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: NONE. All signals (per-letter logprobs on calibration and on each benchmark) already exist in ckpts/gate_7b_pmctrain_prune/cap320 and ckpts/gate_7b_prune/cap320.
methods.expected_strength: Beats a raw margin threshold when the cheap model's softmax is mis-calibrated across benchmarks: the conformal quantile re-anchors the set boundary to a target error rate using calibration labels, so the 'keep at 7B' region is the set of inputs where the true answer is conformally covered by a singleton, not just where the top1-top2 gap is large. Set-size deferral is scale-free across the 4-6 benchmarks and FBE adapts the operating point, which should reduce escalation below 63% at the same accuracy when margin and true-error are weakly coupled (the regime your margin gate is stuck in).

methods.name: Training-Free Conformal Deferral (set-size singleton deferral)
methods.paper: No Need for Learning to Defer? A Training-Free Deferral Framework to Multiple Experts through Conformal Prediction (arXiv 2509.12573)
methods.mechanism: Wrap the cheap classifier in split conformal prediction (LAC, APS, or RAPS nonconformity scores) calibrated to level 1-alpha. If the prediction set is a singleton (|Gamma_alpha(x)|=1) accept the cheap answer; otherwise DEFER. alpha is grid-searched on a small meta-validation set. (Their multi-expert routing collapses, for a 2-stage cascade, to 'defer the non-singletons to the strong model'.)
methods.signal_required: Cheap-model softmax/logprobs over the label set (single decode). Calibration uses (x, y_true) pairs; no expert/strong-model annotations on the calibration set.
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: YES. Identical signal to CP-Router: our 7B per-letter logprobs give LAC (1 - p(true)), APS, and RAPS scores; calibration quantile from 7B-on-PMC-train correctness labels; deferral = escalate any non-singleton set. The 'highest-segregativity expert' selection step is unneeded with a single strong model. No 32B labels required.
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: NONE. Uses the same already-saved 7B logprob checkpoints; only a small held-out slice of PMC-train is needed to grid-search alpha.
methods.expected_strength: Same family advantage as CP-Router but lets you sweep LAC vs APS vs RAPS. RAPS in particular shrinks set sizes for confident inputs and so produces MORE singletons (less escalation) than a margin rule when the softmax has a heavy tail of near-tied options - common in 4-5-way med-VQA. Wins on compute-saving when many questions are 'clearly 2-way ambiguous' (margin would escalate) but RAPS still certifies a singleton at the chosen alpha.

methods.name: Conformal Risk Control (CRC)
methods.paper: Conformal Risk Control (Angelopoulos, Bates, Fisch, Lei, Schuster), ICLR 2024 (arXiv 2208.02814)
methods.mechanism: Pick the escalation threshold lambda (e.g. on the cheap model's margin or 1-maxprob) by the CRC rule: choose the smallest lambda whose empirical risk on the calibration set, inflated by a 1/n finite-sample term, stays <= alpha, where the risk is a monotone loss (e.g. cheap-model error rate on kept inputs). Guarantee: E[L(lambda)] <= alpha. This turns 'choose tau' into 'choose tau with a provable bound on the kept-set error'.
methods.signal_required: Any monotone scalar confidence on the cheap model (margin, maxprob, energy, entropy) PLUS a loss computable on calibration data (cheap-model correctness). No strong-model signal needed.
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: YES. CRC is a calibration wrapper around your existing margin signal. Our 7B logprobs give margin/maxprob/entropy; our calibration (7B-on-PMC-train with its own correctness) is exactly the (score, loss) pairs CRC needs. You replace the heuristic tau=0.426 with the CRC-selected lambda that provably bounds the kept-at-7B error rate at level alpha. Strong-model labels not required because the controlled risk is the CHEAP model's error on inputs it keeps.
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: NONE. Pure post-hoc recomputation on the existing 7B calibration and eval checkpoints.
methods.expected_strength: Does not by itself beat margin on the SAME signal (it IS a margin threshold, just principled) - its win is replacing your held-out-tuned tau with a tau carrying a finite-sample kept-set-error guarantee, which lets you push the operating point to the largest lambda the guarantee allows. Concretely it lets you ESCALATE LESS while certifying the 7B-kept error stays at the 32B-error level; the heuristic tau=0.426 is likely conservative, so CRC at the binding alpha can lower escalation below 63% at iso-accuracy. Strongest when paired with a better score than margin (e.g. set-size).

methods.name: Learn then Test (LTT) for threshold selection
methods.paper: Learn then Test: Calibrating Predictive Algorithms to Achieve Risk Control (Angelopoulos, Bates, Candes, Jordan, Lei), arXiv 2110.01052
methods.mechanism: Treat each candidate escalation threshold lambda as a hypothesis 'risk(lambda) <= alpha', compute a valid p-value per lambda (e.g. Hoeffding/Bentkus on calibration losses), and use multiple-testing control (fixed-sequence testing along an ordered lambda grid) to return the set of thresholds that provably control risk with high probability 1-delta. You then take the most compute-saving valid threshold.
methods.signal_required: Cheap-model scalar score (margin/maxprob/set-size) and a bounded loss on calibration data (cheap-model correctness). No strong-model signal.
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: YES. LTT is again a calibration-only wrapper over your existing margin (or set-size) score using 7B-on-PMC-train correctness as the loss. It gives a *high-probability* (not just in-expectation) guarantee on the 7B-kept error, then picks the threshold that escalates least among those that pass. No 32B calibration labels needed since the controlled risk is the cheap leg's own error.
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: NONE. Post-hoc on existing checkpoints. (Optional: a slightly larger PMC-train calibration sample tightens the Bentkus p-values, but the existing 3,000-row calibration set is usable.)
methods.expected_strength: Same as CRC but with a stronger per-run guarantee (delta), which is the property Trust-or-Escalate highlights. It beats a naively-tuned margin when you need a *certified* operating point and want the least-escalation threshold that survives multiple testing; in practice it formalizes 'how low can tau go' and typically returns a less conservative tau than a single held-out point estimate, saving compute at iso-accuracy.

methods.name: Cascaded Selective Evaluation (Trust or Escalate)
methods.paper: Trust or Escalate: LLM Judges with Provable Guarantees for Human Agreement, ICLR 2025 (arXiv 2407.18370)
methods.mechanism: Cheap judge answers; estimate its confidence via 'Simulated Annotators' (sample multiple in-context annotator personas and count agreement) rather than raw logprobs. Escalate to the strong judge when confidence < lambda. lambda is calibrated by fixed-sequence testing (LTT-style) so that P(cheap decision agrees with human | cheap decides) >= 1-alpha with high probability per run.
methods.signal_required: Multiple sampled cheap-model outputs (the simulated-annotator ensemble) to form a confidence; calibration needs HUMAN-agreement labels (here: ground-truth correctness). Strong model not needed at calibration.
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: PARTIAL. The calibration/threshold machinery (fixed-sequence testing on cheap-model correctness) maps cleanly onto our 7B-on-PMC-train labels. But the core 'Simulated Annotators' confidence requires MULTIPLE sampled 7B outputs per question (different in-context personas / temperature samples); our checkpoints have only a single greedy decode with logprobs. You could substitute the logprob-margin as the confidence and keep their LTT calibration (then it reduces to LTT above), but reproducing their actual confidence estimator is not possible from saved data.
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: Simulated-annotator confidence needs a 7B re-run with multiple in-context-persona / temperature samples per question (e.g. k samples) to count agreement. The threshold calibration itself needs no re-run.
methods.expected_strength: Beats a margin threshold when the cheap model's single-decode logprob is poorly calibrated (its main claim: simulated annotators cut ECE ~50% and raised coverage). For our reasoning-style 7B whose greedy margin may be over/under-confident, a sampled-agreement confidence can keep more questions at 7B at the same accuracy than margin, lowering escalation. The cost is k extra cheap forward passes, which only pays off if k*cost(7B) << saved 32B calls.

methods.name: C3PO (Cascades with Probabilistic Cost Constraints)
methods.paper: C3PO: Optimized Large Language Model Cascades with Probabilistic Cost Constraints for Reasoning (arXiv 2511.07396)
methods.mechanism: Per-model confidence thresholds tau_j; cascade exits at the first model with s_j >= tau_j. Thresholds are chosen by grid search under a conformal cost constraint: accept a tau-vector only if the (1-alpha)-quantile of per-query cost on calibration data <= budget C*. Guarantee (Thm 1): P(C_test > C*) <= alpha under exchangeability. Crucially uses SELF-SUPERVISED agreement (cheap-vs-strong prediction match) instead of ground-truth labels.
methods.signal_required: Cheap-model confidence score s (margin/maxprob), plus self-supervision pairs = cheap prediction vs strong (MPM) prediction on a calibration set (label-free but needs strong-model PREDICTIONS on calibration). Per-query cost values.
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: PARTIAL. The conformal cost-constraint calibration and the s_j>=tau_j exit are directly implementable (we have 7B confidence and per-cap token/FLOP costs in token_cache.json). The blocker is the self-supervised signal: it needs the 32B's PREDICTIONS on the SAME calibration inputs (PMC-train) to measure 7B-vs-32B agreement, and we only ran 32B on the 8,220-sample eval set, not on PMC-train. On the eval set we DO have both predictions, so an offline analysis is possible there, but a clean held-out calibration would need 32B-on-PMC-train.
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: 32B-on-PMC-train predictions (think mode) to get the self-supervised 7B-vs-32B agreement labels for calibration. No logprobs from 32B are needed (only its predicted letter), so this is feasible.
methods.expected_strength: Flips the control target from accuracy to COST: it directly guarantees P(cost > budget) <= alpha, which is exactly your 'maximize compute saving' objective. It beats a margin-accuracy threshold when you want to pin a compute budget (e.g. 'never exceed 60% of always-32B FLOPs with 90% prob') and squeeze the most accuracy under it, rather than fixing accuracy and hoping cost falls. Self-supervised agreement also escalates only where 7B and 32B actually disagree, which can undercut margin's 63% escalation.

methods.name: Cost-Saving LLM Cascades with Early Abstention
methods.paper: Cost-Saving LLM Cascades with Early Abstention (arXiv 2502.09054)
methods.mechanism: Standard confidence-threshold cascade, but the cheap stage may ABSTAIN early (drop the query entirely) when it anticipates that even the expensive model would be wrong/abstain, exploiting cross-model error correlation - avoiding the wasted strong-model call. Thresholds chosen by cost/loss minimization on a held-out set.
methods.signal_required: Cheap-model confidence/uncertainty score; to learn the early-abstention rule it uses correlations between cheap and strong model error patterns (needs strong-model correctness on a held-out set).
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: PARTIAL. Threshold tuning uses our 7B confidence. The early-abstention rule needs the joint (7B-correct, 32B-correct) distribution to estimate where escalation is futile; we have this on the 8,220-eval set (both legs ran) but NOT on PMC-train calibration. So an offline study on eval is possible, but a clean calibrated abstention rule needs 32B-on-PMC-train. Note: early abstention only helps if your task tolerates skipping queries - in forced-choice med-VQA you must answer, so the 'abstain' branch maps to 'keep 7B answer even though low-confidence' rather than dropping it.
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: 32B-on-PMC-train correctness labels to estimate cheap-vs-strong error correlation for the calibration split. No logprobs needed from 32B.
methods.expected_strength: Beats plain margin escalation specifically by NOT escalating questions the 32B would also get wrong (the futile-escalation set). Since your 32B is near-chance on MedXpert and only 0.572 overall, a non-trivial fraction of escalations buy nothing; identifying and short-circuiting them directly cuts 32B calls at iso-accuracy. This is the most targeted attack on your 'escalate 63%, save only 26%' problem.

methods.name: CALM-style per-step risk control (LTT for early exit)
methods.paper: Confident Adaptive Language Modeling (Schuster, Fisch et al.), NeurIPS 2022 (arXiv 2207.07061)
methods.mechanism: Calibrate a local exit/confidence threshold lambda via Learn-then-Test (distribution-free risk control) so that a global sequence-level quality metric is provably maintained at level 1-epsilon with prob 1-delta. Local confidence measured by softmax top-2 difference, hidden-state cosine saturation, or a small early-exit classifier.
methods.signal_required: Per-step cheap confidence (top-2 softmax gap is the cheapest variant); calibration needs the quality metric computable on calibration data (ground-truth correctness).
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: PARTIAL. The relevant transfer is the CALIBRATION recipe (LTT to pick a threshold with a provable quality guarantee) applied at the question level to our 7B top-2 softmax gap = our margin. That part is fully implementable on saved 7B logprobs + PMC-train correctness, and is essentially the LTT entry instantiated with margin as the score. The hidden-state-saturation and trained-classifier confidence variants are NOT available (we did not save 7B hidden states for the cap320 cascade run; feats_full is from the killed routing direction at full res, layer 14).
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: NONE for the softmax-gap variant (uses existing logprobs). The hidden-state or learned-classifier confidence variants would need a 7B re-run dumping layer activations at cap320.
methods.expected_strength: Mainly a principled-threshold win identical to LTT/CRC: it certifies that keeping a question at 7B preserves quality at level 1-epsilon, letting you choose the least-escalation threshold that passes. The distinctive upside is its richer confidence options (hidden-state saturation) which historically separate easy from hard better than raw softmax gap - but only if you re-run to capture them; on saved data it collapses to margin+LTT.

methods.name: FrugalGPT cascade (DistillBERT scorer baseline; non-conformal)
methods.paper: FrugalGPT: How to Use LLMs While Reducing Cost and Improving Performance (Chen, Zaharia, Zou), arXiv 2305.05176
methods.mechanism: Sequential cascade: query the cheapest model first; a learned scoring function judges whether the answer is 'good enough'; if its score exceeds a per-model threshold, return it, else escalate. Thresholds + model order optimized to minimize cost subject to an accuracy target on a held-out set. No finite-sample / conformal guarantee.
methods.signal_required: A learned answer-quality score (FrugalGPT trains a DistilBERT scorer on the cheap model's generated answer text); thresholds tuned on held-out labels including strong-model outcomes.
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: PARTIAL/NO as published. Pure threshold-tuning is doable, but the defining component is a TRAINED scorer over the generated answer, which (a) requires training and (b) needs the cheap model's full generated text, not just the answer letter logprobs we saved. It is the canonical NON-conformal baseline to contrast against; included for completeness as the family's reference point, not as a training-free option.
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: To reproduce faithfully: a labeled set to TRAIN the scorer, plus the cheap model's generated answer text (we have raw_output but the scorer also needs training). Strong-model correctness on calibration for threshold tuning.
methods.expected_strength: A trained scorer can in principle outscore a fixed margin because it learns a nonlinear good-enough predictor from text - but it sacrifices the training-free property and the finite-sample guarantee. It is the comparison point that justifies the conformal methods: included to show why the calibration-only conformal variants (CP-Router, CRC/LTT) are preferred for your stated training-free constraint.

methods.name: Edge-Cloud Cascade via Conformal Alignment (CAb cascading)
methods.paper: Reliable Inference in Edge-Cloud Model Cascades via Conformal Alignment (Huang, Park, Simeone, Paoletti), arXiv 2510.17543
methods.mechanism: Cast escalation as multiple-hypothesis testing: learn an alignment-score predictor that judges whether the edge model's prediction set Gamma^e(x) meets the CLOUD model's conditional-coverage standard; calibrate a selection threshold that controls the false-discovery-rate of coverage violations among edge-kept inputs at level (1-delta). Keep at edge only if the input passes the alignment test, else escalate to cloud.
methods.signal_required: Edge (cheap) prediction set from softmax PLUS reference calibration data from the CLOUD model's distribution - i.e. cloud-model outputs on calibration to define the alignment target.
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: NO (cleanly). It explicitly requires the strong/cloud model's outputs during calibration to define conditional-coverage alignment, and trains an alignment-score predictor. We have no 32B outputs on PMC-train calibration and 32B has no logprobs to form a comparison distribution. The cheap-side prediction set is derivable from our 7B logprobs, but the cloud-conditioned alignment target and the FDR-controlled selector are not buildable from saved data.
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: 32B-on-PMC-train outputs (at minimum predicted letters; ideally a distribution, which the reasoning 32B does not emit) to define the alignment criterion, plus training the alignment-score predictor.
methods.expected_strength: When implementable it beats margin by escalating exactly the inputs whose cheap prediction set FAILS to match strong-model-level coverage, with an FDR guarantee on coverage violations - a more targeted escalation than a marginal confidence cut. But for OUR setup the strong model is a logprob-free reasoning model, so the conditional-coverage target is hard to define; this method is a poor fit and is listed mainly to mark the boundary of what our checkpoints support.

families.family_summary: The conformal / risk-controlled deferral family splits into two layers that are both directly relevant to a 7B->32B med-VQA cascade. (1) A calibration LAYER - Conformal Risk Control (ICLR 2024), Learn-then-Test (2021), and the CALM-style per-step LTT (NeurIPS 2022) - which is training-free and turns 'pick tau' into 'pick the least-escalation threshold whose kept-at-7B error is provably bounded at level alpha (in expectation for CRC, or with high probability 1-delta for LTT)'. These need only a scalar cheap-model score plus the cheap model's own correctness on calibration, so they drop straight onto our 7B logprobs + PMC-train labels with NO GPU re-run and replace the heuristic tau=0.426 with a certified, typically less-conservative operating point. (2) A SIGNAL layer - CP-Router (AAAI 2026) and the training-free conformal deferral framework (2026) - which replaces the margin scalar with a conformal PREDICTION-SET-SIZE rule (escalate any non-singleton set under LAC/APS/RAPS at a calibrated alpha, with FBE auto-selecting alpha); these are the best-fit methods because they use exactly our available signal (7B per-letter softmax) and exactly our calibration (cheap-model correctness, no 32B labels) and are fully reproducible offline. The frontier then specializes the controlled QUANTITY: C3PO (2025) controls a probabilistic COST budget (P(cost>C*)<=alpha) using label-free 7B-vs-32B agreement, and Early-Abstention cascades (2025) skip futile escalations the 32B would also miss - both directly target your 'escalate 63% but save only 26%' pathology, but require 32B predictions on the PMC-train calibration split (a feasible re-run since 32B's predicted letter, not logprobs, is enough). Methods that need strong-model confidence distributions or trained scorers (Edge-Cloud Conformal Alignment; FrugalGPT's DistilBERT scorer) are poor fits because our 32B is a logprob-free reasoning model. Net: CP-Router and CRC/LTT are immediately implementable and most likely to beat a raw margin threshold at iso-accuracy, because they re-anchor or replace the (mis-calibrated, benchmark-varying) margin signal with a calibration-certified set-size or risk-controlled cutoff.

methods.name: Maximum Softmax Probability (MSP / MaxProb) over answer-choice tokens
methods.paper: Plaut, Khanna et al., "Softmax Probabilities (Mostly) Predict Large Language Model Correctness on Multiple-Choice Q&A" (also titled "Probabilities of Chat LLMs Are Miscalibrated but Still Predict Correctness on Multiple-Choice Q&A")
methods.mechanism: Take the model's probability of its top-1 answer-choice token from a single forward pass; escalate to the strong model when that max probability falls below a threshold (low confidence = defer). Threshold is picked to hit a target escalation budget / iso-accuracy.
methods.signal_required: Cheap model's top-1 softmax probability over the answer-choice tokens from one greedy forward pass (no samples, no full sequence).
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: YES. Directly derivable from our 7B cap320 opt_logprobs dict: softmax the per-letter logprobs and take the max. No re-run. Threshold can be calibrated on the 7B PMC-train logprobs against the 7B's own correctness exactly as our margin tau is.
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: NONE.
methods.expected_strength: Rarely beats margin and often essentially equivalent in MC settings: MSP and margin are monotonically related when the top-2 dominate. It can differ from margin when the top-1 is high but spread over a flat tail (many near-equal alternatives) -- there margin (top1-top2) stays large while MSP drops, so MSP defers more such cases. It is a fair cheap A/B baseline but unlikely to win much on compute-at-iso-accuracy versus margin.

methods.name: Max Logit (pre-softmax) over answer-choice tokens
methods.paper: Plaut, Khanna et al., "Softmax Probabilities (Mostly) Predict Large Language Model Correctness on Multiple-Choice Q&A"
methods.mechanism: Threshold the raw (un-normalized) logit of the chosen answer token rather than its softmax probability; escalate when the max logit is below threshold. Paper finds max logit correlates with accuracy even more strongly (r=0.95) than MSP across models.
methods.signal_required: Cheap model's raw logit for the chosen answer token, single forward pass.
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: PARTIAL. Our checkpoints store opt_logprobs (log-softmax values), not raw pre-softmax logits, so the absolute logit scale is gone. The relative ranking within a question is preserved, but the cross-question logit magnitude that the paper exploits is not recoverable from saved logprobs. Faithful reproduction needs the raw logits.
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: Cheap 7B re-run at cap320 dumping raw answer-token logits (cheap; greedy, 1 token; same passes we already do) to get true max-logit scale.
methods.expected_strength: Could beat margin on compute-at-iso-accuracy if cross-question logit magnitude carries calibration that log-softmax normalization destroys -- the paper's r=0.95 vs MSP r=0.68 hints the unnormalized scale is more informative. Worth a small re-run as a cheap A/B given the paper's evidence.

methods.name: Predictive Entropy of the answer distribution (single-pass token/option entropy)
