methods.paper: Malinin & Gales, "Uncertainty Estimation in Autoregressive Structured Prediction" (predictive entropy); reused as PE baseline in Kuhn et al. and Duan et al.
methods.mechanism: Compute Shannon entropy of the model's output distribution; escalate when entropy is high (flat distribution = uncertain). For a single-token MC answer this is the entropy of the option-token softmax; for sequences it is the entropy of per-token next-token distributions (mean token entropy).
methods.signal_required: Cheap model's output probability distribution from one forward pass (full per-option softmax for MC; per-token distributions for sequences). No samples needed for the single-pass version.
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: YES (single-pass option-entropy form). We have the full per-letter logprob dict, so H = -sum p_i log p_i over the letters is directly computable, no re-run. The multi-token mean-token-entropy form is NOT available because the 7B emits only 2 tokens (just the letter) and we only store the answer-letter distribution, not full-vocab distributions at each step.
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: NONE for the option-entropy form.
methods.expected_strength: Beats margin when the uncertainty lives in the tail/shape of the option distribution rather than in the top-2 gap -- e.g. a question where 3-4 options are all plausible: margin (top1-top2) can look confident while entropy correctly flags it. On our 8+ letter dicts (often padded with near-zero-prob distractors) entropy is dominated by the few real options, so in practice it tends to track margin; modest, situational gains. Cheapest possible alternative signal to A/B.

methods.name: Length-normalized sequence (log)probability / Length-normalized Predictive Entropy (LN-PE)
methods.paper: Malinin & Gales (length-normalization for NLG); used as LN-PE baseline in Duan et al. SAR and as "Chow-Average" in Gupta et al. cascades
methods.mechanism: Average the per-token log-probabilities of the single generated answer over its length (geometric-mean token probability); escalate when this normalized confidence is below threshold. Length normalization removes the bias whereby longer generations always look less probable.
methods.signal_required: Per-token logprobs of one greedy generation, plus its length. Single forward pass, no samples.
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: PARTIAL/degenerate. Our cheap 7B answer is a single letter (gen_tokens=2), so 'length-normalized sequence probability' collapses to just the chosen-letter probability (= a monotone function of MSP). The method only becomes distinct from MSP if the cheap leg generates a multi-token answer/rationale. So on the current no-think single-letter checkpoints it adds nothing beyond MSP.
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: To make it non-degenerate: re-run the cheap 7B in a short free-text or short-chain mode (multi-token answer) at cap320 and store per-token logprobs. This changes the cheap-leg cost, so it competes against a no-think baseline only if the extra tokens are few.
methods.expected_strength: Would beat margin only in a regime where the cheap model produces multi-token answers and the per-token probabilities (not just the final letter) carry the difficulty signal. In our current single-letter MC setup it is dominated by margin/MSP. Documented to 'overcorrect' length bias (Gupta et al.).

methods.name: Chow-Sum (max/total sequence log-probability, Chow's rule)
methods.paper: Gupta, Narasimhan, Jitkrittum, Rawat, Menon, Kumar, "Language Model Cascades: Token-level uncertainty and beyond", ICLR
methods.mechanism: Deferral score = total sequence log-probability of the cheap model's greedy answer (classic Chow's reject rule extended to sequences); escalate when the sequence log-prob is low. Shown to suffer length bias (favors deferring long or short sequences regardless of quality).
methods.signal_required: Sum of per-token logprobs of one greedy generation. Single forward pass, no samples.
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: PARTIAL/degenerate, same reason as LN-PE: with a single-letter answer the sequence log-prob is just the letter's logprob (monotone in MSP). Distinct only for multi-token cheap-leg answers.
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: Same as LN-PE: needs a multi-token cheap-leg generation to be non-degenerate.
methods.expected_strength: Provided as the baseline that the cascade paper's learned token-level rules beat; on single-letter MC it is dominated by margin/MSP and additionally carries length bias. Useful only as a named baseline, not expected to win.

methods.name: Chow-Quantile + learned token-level deferral rule
methods.paper: Gupta et al., "Language Model Cascades: Token-level uncertainty and beyond", ICLR
methods.mechanism: Extract quantiles/percentiles of the cheap model's per-token probabilities (richer than a single aggregate) and feed them, optionally with Chow-Sum/Average, into a small post-hoc deferral classifier (logistic regression / small MLP) trained to predict whether deferral helps; escalate when the classifier's deferral score exceeds threshold.
methods.signal_required: Per-token probability vector of one greedy generation (to form quantiles) + a trained deferral head. Single forward pass for the signal; supervised training for the rule.
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: NO (as intended) on two counts: (1) the cheap answer is a single token so there is no per-token quantile distribution to summarize; (2) it requires a trained deferral classifier, and crucially its target label is 'does escalation flip wrong->right', which needs 32B correctness ALIGNED to cheap-model uncertainty on the calibration set -- we have NO 32B labels on PMC-train calibration. A degenerate single-feature version reduces to thresholding MSP.
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: Both: (a) multi-token cheap-leg generation with per-token logprobs, and (b) 32B-on-PMC-train labels to supervise the deferral head against true escalation benefit. Both are GPU re-runs.
methods.expected_strength: This is the paper's headline win: learned token-level rules beat simple aggregation, and a calibrated token-margin becomes near-optimal. It would beat our margin threshold precisely when difficulty is encoded across the answer's token trajectory and when the deferral rule is trained on real 32B-vs-7B benefit -- neither of which our current single-letter, 32B-unlabeled-calibration setup supports without re-runs.

methods.name: TokenSAR (relevance-weighted length-normalized log-prob)
methods.paper: Duan, Cheng, Wang et al., "Shifting Attention to Relevance: Towards the Uncertainty Estimation of Large Language Models" (SAR), ACL 2024
methods.mechanism: Generalizes length-normalized log-prob by weighting each token's negative log-prob by its semantic relevance (how much removing the token changes the sentence meaning, via a similarity model), then escalate on high relevance-weighted uncertainty. Down-weights filler tokens that inflate naive entropy.
methods.signal_required: Per-token logprobs of one greedy generation PLUS a token-relevance score from an auxiliary sentence-similarity / cross-encoder model. Single LLM forward pass, but an extra small encoder pass per token.
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: NO. TokenSAR needs a multi-token free-form answer to have relevant-vs-irrelevant tokens to reweight; our cheap leg emits a single answer letter, so relevance weighting is vacuous (one token = full relevance), collapsing it to that letter's logprob (MSP again). Also requires running the auxiliary relevance encoder.
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: Needs a multi-token cheap-leg generation (re-run) plus the auxiliary relevance/similarity encoder; no 32B labels needed (it's a pure cheap-model UQ signal).
methods.expected_strength: Beats margin/entropy when the cheap model produces free-form rationales and naive token uncertainty is diluted by semantically empty tokens -- SAR's whole premise. Irrelevant to single-letter MC, where there is no linguistic redundancy to exploit. Only relevant if the cheap leg is switched to generative answers.

methods.name: SentSAR / SAR (sentence-relevance-weighted, multi-sample)
methods.paper: Duan et al., "Shifting Attention to Relevance" (SAR), ACL 2024
methods.mechanism: Sample K generations, weight each sample's probability by its semantic similarity to the other samples (relevant/agreeing samples get more weight), aggregate into a sentence-level uncertainty; SAR combines TokenSAR + SentSAR. Escalate on high uncertainty.
methods.signal_required: K sampled generations (paper uses K=5-10) with their logprobs + a similarity model. Requires multiple stochastic samples.
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: NO. Requires K stochastic samples per question; we have a single greedy decode only. Also needs multi-token generations and an auxiliary similarity model.
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: Temperature sampling of K generations from the 7B (multiplies cheap-leg cost by ~K) plus the similarity encoder. This directly undercuts the compute-saving goal unless K is tiny.
methods.expected_strength: Strong UQ in free-form QA literature, but the K-sample cost is antithetical to a compute-saving cascade: spending K cheap forward passes to decide escalation only pays off if it slashes escalation rate enough to beat both the K-sample overhead and a 1-sample margin. Unlikely to win on FLOPs-at-iso-accuracy for our single-letter MC task.

methods.name: Semantic Entropy (SE) / length-normalized Semantic Entropy
methods.paper: Kuhn, Gal, Farquhar, "Semantic Uncertainty: Linguistic Invariances for Uncertainty Estimation in Natural Language Generation", ICLR 2023; extended in Farquhar et al., Nature 2024 "Detecting hallucinations using semantic entropy"
methods.mechanism: Sample K generations, cluster them into meaning-equivalence classes using an NLI/entailment model (e.g. DeBERTa-MNLI), then compute entropy over the cluster (meaning) probabilities rather than token sequences; escalate when semantic entropy is high. Length-normalized variant divides sequence log-probs by length before aggregating.
methods.signal_required: K sampled generations (paper: ~5-10, '5 is plenty') with sequence logprobs + an entailment/NLI clustering model. Requires temperature sampling.
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: NO. Needs multiple stochastic samples and meaning-clustering. For single-letter MC, semantic clustering is trivial (each letter is its own cluster) so SE degenerates to the entropy of the empirical letter-frequency over K samples -- which we cannot compute because we have only 1 greedy sample. The single-pass option-entropy we already have is the degenerate K->infinity analytic limit.
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: Temperature sampling of K 7B generations per question (K x cheap-leg cost). NLI model not even needed for MC (clusters = letters), but the K samples are.
methods.expected_strength: SE's advantage is in free-form generation where token entropy conflates surface form with meaning; on single-token MC that advantage vanishes (no surface/meaning gap) and it reduces to sampled letter entropy, which the analytic option-entropy already approximates at zero extra cost. Not expected to beat margin on our task, and the K-sample cost hurts the compute goal.

methods.name: Discrete Semantic Entropy (DSE) / black-box sampled-answer entropy
methods.paper: Farquhar, Kossen, Kuhn, Gal, "Detecting hallucinations in large language models using semantic entropy", Nature 2024 (discrete/black-box variant)
methods.mechanism: Black-box version of SE that does NOT use token probabilities: sample K generations, cluster by meaning, estimate each cluster's probability as its empirical sample frequency, take entropy of that categorical distribution; escalate when high. For MC this is just the entropy of the sampled answer-letter frequencies.
methods.signal_required: K sampled generations only (no logprobs). Requires multiple stochastic samples.
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: NO. Requires K samples; we have 1 greedy decode. The appeal (no logprobs needed) is moot for us since we DO have logprobs but DON'T have samples -- the exact opposite of what DSE assumes.
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: Temperature sampling of K 7B decodes per question.
methods.expected_strength: Designed for the black-box / no-logprob regime, which is not our constraint. For our white-box single-letter setup the analytic option-entropy strictly dominates it (same quantity, computed exactly from logprobs at K=1 cost). No advantage for our cascade.

methods.name: Self-Consistency / sampled-answer agreement (majority-vote frequency)
methods.paper: Wang et al. self-consistency lineage; applied as training-free routing/deferral signal in works such as "In-Context Distillation with Self-Consistency Cascades" and self-consistency-based routing
methods.mechanism: Sample K cheap-model answers; confidence = relative frequency of the majority answer; escalate when agreement is low (samples disagree). No learned components.
methods.signal_required: K stochastic samples of the answer (logprobs optional). Multiple samples required.
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: NO. We have a single greedy sample; agreement needs K stochastic samples. For MC, the analytic option-probability we already store is the expected-agreement signal at K->infinity, so a K-sample run would mostly recover what margin/MSP already encode.
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: Temperature sampling of K 7B decodes per question (K x cheap-leg cost).
methods.expected_strength: Wins over margin mainly on reasoning/free-form tasks where a single greedy logprob is unreliable but sampling reveals instability. For single-token MC with calibrated logprobs, the K-sample agreement is largely redundant with the analytic top-1 probability, and the K-fold cheap cost works against the compute-saving objective. Unlikely to beat margin at iso-FLOPs here.

methods.name: Semantic Entropy Probes (SEP)
methods.paper: Kossen, Han, Razzak, Schut, Malik, Gal, "Semantic Entropy Probes: Robust and Cheap Hallucination Detection in LLMs"
methods.mechanism: Train a linear probe on the cheap model's hidden-state activations (single forward pass) to predict the semantic entropy that would have been computed from K samples; at inference escalate when the probe's predicted entropy is high -- recovering SE's signal at 1-sample cost.
methods.signal_required: Cheap model's hidden-state activations from one forward pass (at inference) + a trained linear probe. Probe TRAINING requires K-sample SE labels on a calibration set.
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: NO. (1) Not training-free -- needs a trained linear probe. (2) We did not save 7B hidden states for these cap320 eval checkpoints (we stored only logprobs/correctness); hidden-state features exist only in feats/ from the killed single-model-routing direction, not aligned to this cascade. (3) Probe labels need K-sample SE on calibration, which we never ran.
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: 7B re-run dumping hidden states on both calibration and eval, plus K-sample SE labels on calibration to train the probe. Substantial.
methods.expected_strength: Would beat margin if the 7B's hidden states encode difficulty that the answer-letter logprobs do not (probe sees representation, not just output). But our own killed single-model-routing audit (oracle ~29 sigma below the luck floor) found one 7B's internal signals carry little routable signal, which is direct local evidence that an internal-state probe is unlikely to beat the output-margin gate here.

methods.name: P(True) self-evaluation confidence
methods.paper: Kadavath et al. (Anthropic), "Language Models (Mostly) Know What They Know"
methods.mechanism: After the cheap model answers, re-prompt it 'Is the proposed answer correct? (a) no (b) yes' and read the probability it assigns to 'yes' (P(True)); escalate when P(True) is low. A second, cheap forward pass used as a self-confidence score.
methods.signal_required: One extra cheap forward pass over a verification prompt, reading the yes/no token probabilities. No samples of the original answer required (though paper shows multi-sample P(True) is better).
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: PARTIAL. The signal is not in our saved checkpoints (we never ran the verification prompt), but it is cheap to add and needs NO 32B labels and NO multi-sample -- just a second 7B greedy pass per question. Calibration of its threshold can use the 7B's own correctness on PMC-train, like our margin tau.
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: A cheap second 7B forward pass per question (verification prompt) to record P(yes). Roughly doubles cheap-leg forward passes but each is short; on PMC-train calibration + eval only.
methods.expected_strength: Beats margin when the model's first-pass answer-distribution is overconfident but its metacognitive self-check is better calibrated -- Kadavath shows P(True) is well-calibrated at scale and improves with self-review. It can flag cases where margin is large but the answer is a confident error. Plausible incremental win, but adds a forward pass; worth testing as a complementary signal to margin (e.g. escalate if margin low OR P(True) low).

families.family_summary: The LLM-uncertainty-for-deferral family splits cleanly along one axis that decides everything for our compute-saving cascade: single-forward-pass signals versus multi-sample signals. Single-pass, training-free signals -- max softmax probability/max logit (Plaut et al. 2024), single-pass predictive/option entropy (Malinin and Gales 2020), and length-normalized or total sequence log-prob / Chow's rule (Gupta et al. ICLR 2024) -- are all directly derivable from our 7B cap320 per-letter logprob dict at zero extra GPU cost, but in a single-token multiple-choice setting they are largely monotone transforms of each other and of our existing margin gate, so they are cheap A/B baselines rather than likely winners. The state-of-the-art accuracy gains in this family come from methods that are either multi-sample (Semantic Entropy and its length-normalized/discrete variants, SentSAR/SAR, self-consistency agreement; K=5-10 stochastic generations plus often an NLI/similarity model) or learned (Chow-Quantile token-level deferral heads, Semantic Entropy Probes on hidden states) -- and crucially their advantage is concentrated in free-form generation where token surface form and meaning diverge, an advantage that collapses on our single-letter MC answers and whose K-sample cost directly fights the compute-saving objective. The methods most worth a controlled re-run on our setup are true max-logit (paper reports r=0.95 vs accuracy, and our saved log-softmax discards the raw logit scale) and P(True) self-evaluation (Kadavath et al. 2022), both single-extra-pass, training-free, and needing no 32B calibration labels; the heavier learned/SE-probe routes are gated by signals we never saved (hidden states, K samples, 32B-on-calibration labels), and our own killed single-model-routing luck-floor audit (~29 sigma below random) is direct local evidence that a 7B internal-state probe is unlikely to beat the output-margin gate.

methods.name: RouteLLM (4 routers: SW-ranking, matrix factorization, BERT classifier, causal-LLM classifier)
methods.paper: RouteLLM: Learning to Route LLMs with Preference Data (ICLR 2025 / arXiv 2406.18665, LMSYS)
methods.mechanism: A router predicts P(strong model wins | query) and escalates to the strong model when that win-probability exceeds a cost threshold alpha; alpha sweeps the strong-call rate. Decision is made BEFORE the cheap model runs, purely from the query.
methods.signal_required: Query text/embedding only. None of the four routers use the cheap model's logprobs, output, or confidence -- confirmed from the paper: 'None of these routers use the weak model's outputs, logprobs, or confidence scores.'
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: PARTIAL. The SW-ranking variant is the only non-trained one (inference-time Bradley-Terry solve), but all four are trained/fit on PAIRWISE PREFERENCE data (which model is better per query). We have no preference labels and -- critically -- no 32B-vs-7B win labels on any calibration set (calib has 7B's own correctness only). To fit even SW-ranking we would need a labeled set of queries with both-model outcomes. It also ignores our richest asset (7B per-letter logprobs), so it cannot exploit the margin signal at all.
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: 32B-on-PMC-train (and ideally 32B + 7B on a held-out routing-train set) to create per-query 'strong-wins' labels; plus an embedding model over queries. No new cheap-model decode needed, but the strong-model labeling pass on calibration data is required.
methods.expected_strength: Beats a margin threshold only when difficulty is predictable from the QUESTION text alone (e.g. whole benchmarks/topics the 7B systematically fails) rather than from per-sample 7B confidence. In our setting the 7B already emits a strong per-sample margin, so a query-only router is unlikely to win on compute-saving unless margin is poorly correlated with 32B-recoverability within a benchmark; its main upside is routing without spending the cheap forward pass.

methods.name: Hybrid LLM (cost-efficient quality-aware query routing; deterministic + probabilistic routers)
methods.paper: Hybrid LLM: Cost-Efficient and Quality-Aware Query Routing (ICLR 2024, Ding et al., Microsoft)
methods.mechanism: A DeBERTa-style router scores each query for the predicted quality gap between small and large model; if the predicted small-model quality is adequate (score over threshold t) keep small, else escalate. A probabilistic-router variant relaxes hard labels (transforms BARTScore gaps into soft targets) to push easy-but-tie queries to the small model. Threshold t trades cost vs quality. Decision is pre-inference, from the query.
methods.signal_required: Query text/embedding only. Router does not read the small model's output or confidence; it predicts the gap from the prompt.
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: PARTIAL/NO. Requires training a router on per-query SMALL-vs-LARGE quality-gap labels (BARTScore gaps). For MCQ we could use correctness-gap (7B right? 32B right?), but we have NO 32B correctness on the calibration split (only 7B-on-PMC-train correctness), so the gap label is unavailable without a 32B calibration pass. Like RouteLLM it ignores our per-letter logprobs.
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: 32B-on-PMC-train (and 7B on the same routing-train queries) to compute per-query correctness/quality gap labels; train the small router. No temperature sampling needed.
methods.expected_strength: Wins over margin when the quality GAP (does 32B actually recover what 7B misses?) is predictable from the query but NOT reflected in 7B confidence -- e.g. 7B confidently wrong on a recoverable topic (margin would keep it; gap-router escalates) or 7B unconfident on something 32B also fails (margin escalates wastefully; gap-router keeps it cheap, saving compute). The gap framing directly targets compute-saving-at-iso-accuracy, which a raw margin (ignoring 32B recoverability) does not.

methods.name: Post-hoc deferral / learning-to-defer estimators (CSS, OvA, post-hoc rejector)
methods.paper: Post-hoc Estimators for Learning to Defer to an Expert (Narasimhan et al., NeurIPS 2022)
methods.mechanism: Train a lightweight deferral (rejector) function ON TOP OF a FIXED base model that predicts to defer when the base model's error probability exceeds the expert's cost c0. Frames deferral as a partial surrogate to the ideal deferral loss; post-hoc training beats cost-sensitive-softmax and one-vs-all at most operating points. Threshold = expert cost.
methods.signal_required: Base (cheap) model's class posterior / confidence features as inputs to the rejector, PLUS the expert's correctness labels on a training set to fit the rejector.
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: PARTIAL. Base model stays frozen and the rejector is a tiny model trained on 7B's per-letter posteriors (which we have). BUT the canonical deferral loss needs the EXPERT's (32B) error/cost on the training set -- we have no 32B labels on the PMC-train calibration split. A degenerate constant-expert-cost version (learning-to-reject) reduces to thresholding 7B's predicted error, which is essentially a calibrated margin and is fully implementable on our 7B logprobs + 7B correctness alone.
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: For the true learning-to-defer objective: 32B-on-PMC-train labels. For the reject-only degenerate form: NONE (uses existing 7B logprobs + 7B correctness).
methods.expected_strength: Beats a fixed margin threshold by learning a deferral surface over richer 7B features (full posterior, not just top1-top2 gap) that better predicts 7B error, and -- when 32B labels exist -- by incorporating expert cost/recoverability so it stops escalating cases 32B also gets wrong. Saves compute at iso-accuracy where margin mis-ranks (e.g. low-margin-but-correct or high-margin-but-32B-unrecoverable cases).

methods.name: Confidence-based cascade deferral + post-hoc deferral rule (when confidence suffices)
methods.paper: When Does Confidence-Based Cascade Deferral Suffice? (Jitkrittum et al., NeurIPS 2023)
methods.mechanism: Analyzes when thresholding the cheap model's max-prob/margin is optimal and shows it fails when the cheap model is overconfident-wrong or when downstream recoverability is heterogeneous. Proposes a calibration-only post-hoc deferral rule that augments confidence with extra features fit on a calibration set (needs the expert's error labels) to better rank which cases to escalate.
methods.signal_required: Cheap model confidence/posterior (max-prob, margin, entropy) as base signal; the improved rule additionally needs the downstream/expert model's error labels on a calibration set.
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: PARTIAL. This paper is the most directly on-point diagnosis of our exact method (margin threshold). The diagnostic half (showing WHERE margin fails) is fully runnable on our 7B logprobs + 7B/32B eval correctness. The improved post-hoc rule needs 32B error labels on the CALIBRATION set, which we do not have (calib is 7B-on-PMC-train with 7B correctness only).
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: 32B-on-PMC-train (expert error labels on the calibration split) to fit the improved post-hoc deferral rule. The plain-confidence baseline needs nothing new.
methods.expected_strength: Directly explains and fixes the margin gate's weakness: it wins precisely when 7B confidence does not track 32B-recoverability -- our symptom is 63% escalation for only 26% compute saving, suggesting margin escalates many cases 32B cannot fix. A recoverability-aware post-hoc rule would stop escalating 32B-unrecoverable low-margin cases, cutting escalation rate at the same accuracy.

methods.name: Chow-Quantile token-level uncertainty + learned post-hoc cascade deferral
methods.paper: Language Model Cascades: Token-level uncertainty and beyond (Gupta et al., 2024)
methods.mechanism: Instead of sequence-level max-prob, defer using QUANTILES of the cheap model's per-token probability distribution over its generated sequence (Chow-Quantile, alpha in {0,0.4,0.8}); a learned post-hoc rule combines quantile features. Threshold on the chosen statistic sets the escalation rate.
methods.signal_required: Cheap model's full per-token logprob sequence over its generated answer; the learned variant additionally needs both models' correctness labels (z=1 iff large correct and small incorrect).
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: NO (for token-level quantiles). Our 7B does a SINGLE greedy decode of just the answer LETTER -- there is no multi-token generated sequence to take quantiles over, so Chow-Quantile is undefined on our checkpoints. The over-the-letter-distribution analogue (entropy/quantiles of the per-letter logprob dict) IS derivable, but that is a single-token statistic, not the paper's token-sequence quantile. The learned post-hoc variant also needs 32B calibration labels we lack.
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: To get genuine token-level quantiles: re-run the 7B emitting full per-token logprobs of a generated rationale/answer (i.e. a longer decode, not single-letter). For the learned combiner: 32B-on-PMC-train labels.
methods.expected_strength: Wins when the answer has uncertain tokens hidden inside an otherwise high-probability sequence -- irrelevant to our single-letter decode, so it offers little over margin UNLESS we switch the 7B to emit a multi-token answer/rationale, at which point min-token-prob can catch confident-looking-but-locally-uncertain answers that margin misses.

methods.name: Confidence-Based Cascading with Calibration (CC) / temperature-scaled confidence advantage
methods.paper: When Models Know When They Do Not Know: Calibration, Cascading, and Cleaning (arXiv 2601.07965); cf. C3 Confidence Calibration Model Cascade (arXiv 2402.15991)
methods.mechanism: Apply post-hoc temperature scaling (and histogram equalization) to make the small (and large) model confidences comparable, then route by the smallest calibrated 'confidence advantage' (large minus small calibrated confidence); escalate when the small model's calibrated confidence is too low.
methods.signal_required: Cheap model logits/posterior (for temperature scaling); the full CC 'confidence advantage' also needs the large model's confidence, and calibration needs ground-truth labels for both models on a validation set.
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: PARTIAL. Temperature-scaling the 7B's per-letter logits and thresholding the CALIBRATED margin/maxprob is fully implementable on our 7B logprobs + 7B correctness on PMC-train (a strict, cheap upgrade to our current raw-margin gate). The cross-model 'confidence advantage' is NOT implementable: the 32B is a reasoning model with EMPTY logprobs, so it has no confidence to calibrate, and we have no 32B calibration labels.
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: For the 7B-side calibrated-confidence cascade: NONE (re-use existing 7B logprobs + correctness). The cross-model advantage variant is blocked entirely (32B has no logprobs).
methods.expected_strength: Beats raw margin when the 7B is miscalibrated/overconfident (well-documented for medical VLMs): temperature scaling spreads out the confidence distribution so the threshold separates correct vs wrong more cleanly, letting a lower escalation rate hold iso-accuracy. Cheapest plausible improvement on our exact pipeline.

methods.name: GATEKEEPER (cascade confidence tuning)
methods.paper: GATEKEEPER: Improving Model Cascades Through Confidence Tuning (OpenReview qYI4fw3g4v)
methods.mechanism: Fine-tune the SMALL model's confidence so it is low exactly when the small model is wrong but the large model would be right (and stays high when small is right or large also fails); at inference defer when tuned confidence < threshold.
methods.signal_required: A labeled training set of small-model and large-model correctness per query; at inference, the tuned small-model confidence.
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: NO. Requires FINE-TUNING the 7B (gradient training of the cheap model), which is outside training-free/calibration-only, and needs per-query 32B correctness labels we do not have on calibration. The frozen-7B spirit of our project is violated.
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: 32B-on-a-training-set labels + a 7B fine-tuning run (gradient training), then re-decode the tuned 7B over eval. Substantial GPU cost.
methods.expected_strength: Strongest in principle at compute-saving-at-iso-accuracy because it directly optimizes the deferral-relevant target (small-wrong-and-large-right) rather than generic confidence -- it would suppress escalations on 32B-unrecoverable cases. But it is the most expensive option and not training-free, so it is a contrast/upper-bound rather than a drop-in for us.

methods.name: AutoMix (few-shot self-verification + POMDP meta-verifier)
methods.paper: AutoMix: Automatically Mixing Language Models (Madaan et al., NeurIPS 2024 / arXiv 2310.12963)
methods.mechanism: The small model answers, then SELF-VERIFIES its own answer via a few-shot prompt (a second generation) to get a noisy verification score; a POMDP-based meta-verifier maps that score (Simple/Complex/Unsolvable) to a route decision, escalating Complex cases and skipping Unsolvable ones to maximize incremental-benefit-per-cost.
methods.signal_required: Cheap model's generated answer + a self-verification generation (verification probability); the POMDP meta-verifier is calibrated using observed verification-vs-correctness outcomes (and benefits from large-model outcomes).
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: NO (as-is). Self-verification requires an EXTRA 7B generation pass (verify the answer), which we never ran -- our checkpoints only contain a single-letter decode and its logprobs. The POMDP also wants large-model outcomes to calibrate the meta-verifier. None of the self-verify signals exist on disk.
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: A 7B self-verification decode (second pass: 'Is this answer correct? yes/no' P(yes)) over all eval + calibration; optionally 32B labels to fit the POMDP. Adds cheap-leg compute, partially offsetting savings.
methods.expected_strength: Beats margin when verification ('is my answer right?') is more discriminative than generation confidence -- plausible for medical MCQ where the 7B is overconfident at decode but a separate verify pass exposes errors. The POMDP's Unsolvable bucket specifically avoids escalating cases 32B also fails, directly improving compute-saving-at-iso-accuracy. Cost: the extra verify pass must be cheaper than the escalations it saves.

methods.name: Self-Consistency cascade (sample-agreement deferral)
methods.paper: In-Context Distillation with Self-Consistency Cascades (arXiv 2512.02543); self-consistency deferral as in FrugalGPT-style cascades
methods.mechanism: Sample the cheap model N times on the same input; if the samples agree (consistency score over threshold) accept the cheap answer, else escalate. Agreement is the confidence proxy; threshold sets escalation rate. No learned components.
methods.signal_required: Multiple stochastic samples (temperature > 0) from the cheap model per query.
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: NO. We have a SINGLE greedy decode per question; there are no multiple samples on disk, and greedy gives identical outputs so agreement is undefined. Calibration also stores only single-decode correctness.
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: Temperature sampling: re-run the 7B with N (e.g. 3-5) samples per question over all eval + calibration to compute agreement. N-fold increase in cheap-leg compute.
methods.expected_strength: Wins over single-decode margin when sampling disagreement captures epistemic uncertainty that a single logit margin misses (e.g. 7B is confidently-but-spuriously peaked on one decode). But for single-token MCQ answers the per-letter softmax already encodes most of the distribution, so self-consistency's marginal gain is small and its Nx cheap-cost likely erases the compute saving -- weak fit for our objective.

methods.name: kNN router (non-parametric utility/cost retrieval)
methods.paper: Rethinking Predictive Modeling for LLM Routing: When Simple kNN Beats Complex Learned Routers (arXiv 2505.12601)
methods.mechanism: Embed the query; retrieve k nearest support queries; average their recorded per-model performance scores and costs; route to the model with best predicted utility (score minus lambda*cost). Decision is pre-inference from the query embedding; no gradient training.
methods.signal_required: Query embedding + a labeled support set of (query embedding, per-model correctness, per-model cost). Does NOT use the cheap model's test-time logprobs/confidence.
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: PARTIAL. Training-free (no gradients) and a strong baseline, but the support set must record BOTH 7B and 32B correctness+cost per support query. We have 7B correctness on PMC-train but NO 32B labels there, so the support set cannot encode 32B utility without a 32B calibration pass. It also ignores the 7B per-letter margin signal at test time.
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: 32B-on-PMC-train (and 7B on the same) to build a support set with both-model outcomes; an embedding model over queries. No new cheap-model decode at test time.
methods.expected_strength: Beats margin when model performance is LOCAL in embedding space -- i.e. clusters of semantically similar medical questions that 32B systematically recovers and 7B systematically misses. It captures cross-model recoverability that a 7B-only margin is blind to, so at iso-accuracy it can avoid escalating neighborhoods where 32B also fails, saving compute. Note: our own luck-floor audit suggests within-model signal is weak, so the win hinges on cross-model locality being real.

methods.name: Cost-Spectrum Contrastive Routing (CSCR) with logit/perplexity fingerprints
methods.paper: Cost-Aware Contrastive Routing for LLMs (Shirkavand et al., arXiv 2508.12491)
methods.mechanism: Train a contrastive encoder (Cost-Spectrum InfoNCE) that maps prompts and per-model 'logit footprints' (open models) / 'perplexity fingerprints' (APIs) into a shared space favoring the cheapest accurate expert within cost bands; at deployment route via a single FAISS kNN lookup, lambda controlling cost.
methods.signal_required: Per-model logit/perplexity fingerprints (computed over diverse probe prompts, from each expert model), prompt embeddings, and per-query correctness+cost labels for contrastive training.
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: NO. The encoder requires contrastive TRAINING with per-query both-model correctness/cost labels (no 32B calib labels for us), and the 32B fingerprint needs the 32B's logits/perplexity -- but our 32B is a reasoning model with EMPTY logprobs, so its logit/perplexity fingerprint cannot be computed. Deployment-time kNN is training-free, but the prerequisite encoder+fingerprints are not buildable from our checkpoints.
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: 32B labels + 32B logit/perplexity fingerprints (needs exposing 32B token logprobs, which the current reasoning-model setup does not emit), plus encoder training. Effectively blocked by the 32B-no-logprobs constraint.
methods.expected_strength: Designed to maximize accuracy-cost tradeoff (claims up to 25% improvement) and is robust to changing the expert pool. Would beat margin by combining query semantics with model fingerprints, but for a fixed 2-model cascade with a logit-less 32B it offers little our simpler margin/Hybrid-LLM routers cannot, and it is the least implementable here.

families.family_summary: The routing / learning-to-defer family splits into two architectural camps. (1) Query-only routers (RouteLLM, Hybrid LLM, kNN-router, CSCR, RouterDC) decide BEFORE the cheap model runs, using only the question text/embedding, and essentially never use the cheap model's logprobs; all of them require per-query labels of which model is right (often both-model correctness or preference data) to fit the router, so on our checkpoints they are blocked by the missing 32B-on-calibration labels (and, for fingerprint methods, the 32B's empty logprobs). (2) Confidence-conditioned deferral methods (post-hoc learning-to-defer of Narasimhan; the 'When Does Confidence Suffice' post-hoc rule; calibrated-confidence cascading CC/C3; token-level Chow-Quantile; GATEKEEPER; AutoMix; self-consistency) decide AFTER the cheap model produces a signal, and are the natural successors to our margin gate. The state of the art for training-free / calibration-only deferral is to (a) calibrate the cheap model's confidence (temperature scaling) before thresholding, and (b) make the deferral rule RECOVERABILITY-aware -- escalate only when the 7B is likely wrong AND the 32B is likely right -- which directly targets compute-saving-at-iso-accuracy and is exactly the gap our raw-margin gate (63% escalation, 26% saving) leaves open. The single most binding constraint for us is the absence of 32B correctness labels on the PMC-train calibration split: every method that beats margin by modeling 32B-recoverability (post-hoc L2D, Hybrid-LLM gap, kNN utility, GATEKEEPER) needs a one-time 32B-on-calibration labeling pass, while the only strictly free upgrade is temperature-scaled / richer-feature confidence on the 7B's existing per-letter logprobs.

methods.name: Chow rules: MaxProb / Entropy / Margin confidence-based deferral
methods.paper: When Does Confidence-Based Cascade Deferral Suffice? (NeurIPS 2023)
methods.mechanism: Compute a scalar confidence on the cheap model and escalate when it falls below a single threshold. Three interchangeable signals: MaxProb (top-1 prob), Negative Entropy of the answer distribution, and Margin (top1-top2 gap). The paper formalizes when this 'Chow rule' is Bayes-optimal and characterizes its failure modes (when small-model error and large-model error are correlated, or under distribution shift / overconfidence).
methods.signal_required: Cheap-model per-option probability distribution (full softmax over answer letters) for a single greedy decode. Margin needs top-2; entropy/maxprob need the full distribution.
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: YES. This is essentially our current method (Margin) plus its two siblings. Our 7B cap320 per-letter logprob dict gives MaxProb, Entropy, and Margin directly with no re-run. Entropy and MaxProb are one-line swaps in the gate; threshold refit on the existing 7B-on-PMC-train calibration (correctness-only labels) is exactly what we already do for tau.
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: NONE. All three derivable from the existing cap320 logprob dicts and calibrated against the existing 7B PMC-train correctness labels.
methods.expected_strength: Entropy uses the full distribution (all 4-5 options) rather than just the top-2 gap, so it discriminates better when probability mass is spread across 3+ options (common in 4/5-way med-VQA) while margin can be fooled by a close top-2 that still leaves a confident answer. This is a near-zero-cost ablation that can only match or beat plain margin; the paper's theory says it wins exactly when the error signal lives in the tail of the distribution, not just the runner-up. Unlikely to be a large win alone but it is the correct baseline-strengthening step and free.

methods.name: Chow-Quantile / Chow-Sum / Chow-Average (token-level uncertainty)
methods.paper: Language Model Cascades: Token-level uncertainty and beyond (Google Research, 2024)
methods.mechanism: Generalizes the Chow rule to generative output by aggregating per-token log-probabilities of the cheap model's generated answer string: Chow-Sum (sum of log-probs, length-biased), Chow-Average (length-normalized mean log-prob), and Chow-Quantile (the alpha-quantile of the per-token probabilities, e.g. the minimum-probability token). Escalate when the chosen aggregate is below threshold. A learned post-hoc variant combines the quantiles + sum + average via a small MLP, but the quantile/sum/average rules themselves are training-free.
methods.signal_required: Per-token log-probabilities of the cheap model's generated answer sequence (not just the final answer-letter softmax).
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: PARTIAL. Our 7B no-think decodes only the answer LETTER (single token), so per-letter logprob == single-token Chow rule, which collapses to the MaxProb/Margin case above (no multi-token sequence to take quantiles over). To get a true multi-token signal we would need the 7B to emit a short rationale or a multi-token answer span and capture its per-token logprobs. The learned-MLP post-hoc variant is also not our setup (we have no 32B-on-calibration labels).
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: 7B re-run that decodes a multi-token answer/rationale and saves per-token logprobs (cheap, no-think, single greedy sample). Without that, this degenerates to the single-token Chow rule already covered.
methods.expected_strength: Wins over single-letter margin only when the cheap model emits multiple tokens whose min-probability ('weakest link') token is a better failure predictor than the final letter's margin. For our pure single-letter decode there is no extra token signal, so it would beat plain margin only if we add a short generated span; the 'min-token-prob' quantile is the most promising aggregate per their results.

methods.name: Energy / free-energy (logsumexp) deferral score
methods.paper: Energy-based Out-of-distribution Detection (NeurIPS 2020); applied as a cascade deferral signal
methods.mechanism: Replace the softmax-normalized confidence with the free energy E(x) = -T log sum_i exp(z_i / T) computed over the answer-option logits. Lower energy (higher logsumexp) = more confident; escalate when energy is above threshold. Avoids softmax normalization so it is less fooled by overconfident, peaky distributions and captures absolute logit magnitude.
methods.signal_required: Raw per-option logits of the cheap model (un-normalized). Temperature T is a single calibration scalar.
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: PARTIAL. We store per-letter LOGPROBS (log-softmax), not raw logits. Energy over log-probs is recoverable up to the (per-sample) log-partition constant only if we also stored that constant; from log-probs alone the logsumexp is exactly 0 (they are already normalized), so true energy needs raw pre-softmax logits. Our repo already tested an FBE/energy gate offline (src/analysis/ablations/gate_ablation_bakeoff.py, recompute_energy.py) and it LOST to margin, which is consistent with energy needing raw logits we did not fully retain.
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: 7B re-run saving RAW option logits (not log-softmax) for the answer position, to compute true free energy. Cheap single greedy pass.
methods.expected_strength: Beats margin when failures correlate with low overall logit mass (the model is uncertain across ALL options, an OOD-like 'none fit' signal) rather than a close top-2. Useful for the harder benchmarks (PathVQA) where the model is broadly unsure. Our own bake-off already found it underperforms margin on the current checkpoints, so expected upside is low unless re-run with raw logits.

methods.name: Agreement-Based Cascading (ABC)
methods.paper: Agreement-Based Cascading for Efficient Inference (Kolawole et al., 2024/2025)
methods.mechanism: Maintain an ensemble at the cheap tier; escalate when ensemble members DISAGREE. Two rules: voting-based (defer if the top-vote fraction is below theta_v) and score-based (defer if mean confidence below theta_s). Thresholds estimated from ~100 validation samples. Replaces a single model's (possibly miscalibrated) confidence with cross-member agreement.
methods.signal_required: Multiple cheap predictions per query, either from an ensemble of cheap models or multiple stochastic samples of one cheap model. Just the predicted labels suffice (votes); optionally their confidences.
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: NO as-is (we have a single greedy 7B sample and one 7B model). We have no second cheap model and only one deterministic decode, so there is no disagreement to measure. Could be approximated by sampling the 7B at multiple resolution caps (cap160/320/640) as an 'ensemble of views' since those checkpoints exist, or by temperature sampling.
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: Either temperature/multi-sample 7B decoding (k samples per question), or treat the already-computed multi-cap 7B runs (cap160/320/640) as ensemble members and measure cross-cap agreement (no new GPU needed for the latter, just an offline join of existing prune-sweep checkpoints).
methods.expected_strength: Beats a single margin threshold when the cheap model is poorly calibrated (its confidence does not track correctness) but its INSTABILITY does, e.g. flips answer across resolutions/samples on hard items. The clinical-VQA finding that confidence degrades exactly where accuracy is low (PathVQA) is precisely where agreement can still carry signal. Strong candidate via the free multi-cap-agreement variant; the cost is k cheap forward passes vs 1.

methods.name: Self-Consistency Cascades (in-context distillation)
methods.paper: In-Context Distillation with Self-Consistency Cascades (2025)
methods.mechanism: Draw k samples from the cheap model; if all sampled answers agree, keep the cheap answer, otherwise escalate to the strong model. Self-consistency (sample agreement) is the deferral signal. Training-free; no verifier or router network.
methods.signal_required: k stochastic samples (temperature > 0) of the cheap model's answer per query; compare for unanimity / majority margin.
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: NO as-is. Our 7B run is a single greedy decode (temperature 0), so self-consistency cannot be computed without re-sampling. The per-letter logprob dict is a cheap proxy (predictive entropy approximates expected sample disagreement) but is not the same signal.
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: Temperature-sampled 7B decoding, k samples per question (k=5-10 typical), cap320 no-think. Multiplies cheap-leg cost by k but the cheap leg is small.
methods.expected_strength: Beats margin when answer STABILITY under sampling separates correct from incorrect better than the single-pass probability gap, especially on multiple-choice where a confident-but-wrong greedy answer still flips under sampling. The downside is k cheap passes; net compute win requires that k*cost(7B) + escalations*cost(32B) < margin-gate cost, which holds only because 7B is far cheaper than 32B. Promising for our 63%-escalation problem if sampling reveals many 'confidently wrong' items the margin gate currently keeps.

methods.name: AutoMix (few-shot self-verification + POMDP meta-router)
methods.paper: AutoMix: Automatically Mixing Language Models (NeurIPS 2024)
methods.mechanism: The cheap model verifies its OWN answer via a few-shot self-verification prompt ('is this answer correct given the context? Y/N'), yielding a noisy correctness probability. A POMDP-based meta-verifier denoises this self-verification probability into a route/keep/escalate decision. No verifier training; uses few-shot prompting only.
methods.signal_required: A second cheap forward pass: the cheap model re-prompted to self-verify its answer, producing a Y/N (or its probability). Optionally a context to verify against.
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: PARTIAL. The POMDP meta-router is light and could be fit on our calibration set, but the core SELF-VERIFICATION signal requires a second 7B pass with a verification prompt that we have not run. Our checkpoints contain only the first answer pass, no self-verify Y/N logprob.
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: One extra cheap 7B forward pass per question running the few-shot self-verification prompt (capture P(Y)). Plus offline fit of the POMDP thresholds on calibration (no GPU).
methods.expected_strength: Beats a raw margin threshold when the model's META-judgment of its own answer is better calibrated than its first-pass option probabilities, which is often true for instruction-tuned models. Self-verification can catch confidently-wrong answers (high margin, wrong) that a margin gate keeps, directly attacking our over-keeping/over-escalating tradeoff. Cost is ~2x cheap passes. The POMDP step matters because raw self-verify is noisy.

methods.name: Cost-Saving LLM Cascades with Early Abstention
methods.paper: Cost-Saving LLM Cascades with Early Abstention (Zellinger & Thomson, 2025)
methods.mechanism: Each tier gets TWO thresholds: a deferral threshold phi and a lower abstention threshold xi. If confidence > phi answer; if xi < conf < phi defer up; if conf < xi ABSTAIN immediately instead of paying to escalate (because very-low-confidence items will likely fail at the strong model too). Thresholds set by minimizing P(error & not abstain) + lambda_cost*E[cost] + lambda_abs*P(abstain) via continuous optimization; confidence calibrated by logistic regression.
methods.signal_required: A calibrated cheap-model confidence (maxprob for multiple choice). Needs labeled calibration data, and to set xi optimally it benefits from knowing the strong model's failure correlation.
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: PARTIAL (calibration-only, not full). The maxprob confidence is available from our cap320 logprobs and we can calibrate logistic regression on the 7B PMC-train correctness labels. BUT optimal abstention needs the joint cheap/strong error distribution, and we have NO 32B labels on calibration. We can still fit the deferral threshold and a conservative abstain threshold from cheap-only stats.
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: To use abstention properly: 32B labels on the PMC-train calibration split (32B-on-calib), so the joint copula model can decide which low-confidence items are hopeless. Without it, only the (already-known) deferral half is reproducible.
methods.expected_strength: Saves compute beyond a single margin threshold by NOT escalating the lowest-confidence items the strong model would also get wrong, i.e. it removes wasted 32B calls. This directly targets our '63% escalation, only 26% saving' problem. But it changes the contract from 'always answer' to 'allowed to abstain', which our parity claim (must match 32B accuracy on all items) does not currently permit; only useful if the paper accepts a small abstain budget.

methods.name: Conformal / CP-Router selective deferral
methods.paper: Adaptive Routing with conformal calibration (as used in LazyMCoT / Focus When Necessary, 2026; conformal-prediction cascade routing)
methods.mechanism: Calibrate the escalation threshold by a conformal quantile: set s_floor = the alpha-quantile of cheap-model confidence scores on a calibration set so that AT MOST an alpha fraction of must-keep (correct) samples fall below it. This gives a distribution-free coverage guarantee on the keep set, rather than a hand-tuned tau. Routing score can be any cheap signal (margin/maxprob/first-token gap).
methods.signal_required: Any cheap per-sample confidence score plus a calibration set with correctness labels to take the conformal quantile.
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: YES. We already have the cheap confidence (margin/maxprob/entropy) and a calibration set (7B on PMC-train with its own correctness labels). Replacing the fixed tau=0.426 with a conformal quantile at a target risk alpha is a pure post-processing change. Our repo even has conformal gate ablations (gate_alt_conformal*.py, router_conformal_6ds.pkl) already.
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: NONE. Pure recalibration on existing checkpoints.
methods.expected_strength: Does not change the score, only how the threshold is chosen, so it rarely beats a well-tuned margin tau on raw compute-saving; its win is a GUARANTEE (controlled error/coverage) and better transfer across the 6 benchmarks than a single global tau. Our own bake-off found conformal among the losing gates, so expected compute upside vs our tuned margin is small; value is statistical rigor, not efficiency.

methods.name: First-token / option-logit-gap adaptive routing (single forward pass)
methods.paper: Focus When Necessary: Adaptive Routing and Collaborative Grounding for Training-Free Visual Grounding (LazyMCoT, 2026)
methods.mechanism: From a single forward pass, extract two zero-cost first-answer-token statistics: option top-probability (mass on the top valid option) and option-vs-non-option logit gap (Delta-logit: confidence in choosing a valid letter over any other vocabulary token). Feed them to a tiny GBDT to produce a routing score, thresholded by conformal calibration. Training-free w.r.t. the base VLM (only the light GBDT is fit on calibration).
methods.signal_required: First-answer-token logits over the full vocabulary (to compute option-mass and option-vs-non-option gap), single greedy pass.
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: PARTIAL. We have per-LETTER logprobs (mass among valid options) so option-top-prob and option-margin are available. The distinctive Delta-logit (valid-option vs ALL non-option tokens) needs the full-vocabulary first-token distribution, which we did not save (we only kept the letter subset). The GBDT-over-signals piece is exactly our existing 'learned gate' ablation family (gate_alt_learned_gbm*.py).
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: 7B re-run saving the FULL first-token logit vector (or at least the non-option mass / top non-option logit) so the option-vs-non-option gap can be computed. Cheap single pass.
methods.expected_strength: Beats margin when 'is the model even answering with a valid option' (option-vs-junk gap) predicts failure better than the gap among options, e.g. on hard/ill-posed med items where the model's mass leaks to non-letter tokens. Adds a genuinely new signal (non-option leakage) our letter-only margin cannot see. Most promising of the single-pass training-free signals because it needs no extra decode, only a richer logit save, and matches our existing GBDT bake-off harness.

methods.name: Bi-directional cascading with proxy confidence
methods.paper: Bi-directional Model Cascading with Proxy Confidence (Warren & Dras, 2025)
methods.mechanism: Decide escalation using BOTH directions: (a) cheap-model post-invocation confidence enriched via its hidden states, and (b) a tiny proxy model that PRE-estimates the strong model's confidence before invoking it. Escalate only when the cheap model is unsure AND the proxy predicts the strong model would do better, avoiding escalations that will not pay off.
methods.signal_required: Cheap-model hidden states (for enriched confidence) plus a small learned proxy that predicts strong-model success from the input. Needs strong-model labels to train the proxy.
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: NO. We deliberately do NOT have 32B logprobs/hidden states, and (critically) no 32B labels on the calibration split, so the proxy that predicts 32B success cannot be trained. Cheap-model hidden states for the 7B were extracted only for the killed single-model-routing direction (feats/, feats_full L14), not for the live cascade.
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: 32B-on-PMC-train labels (to train the strong-model-success proxy) AND 7B hidden-state extraction on the live eval set. Both are non-trivial re-runs.
methods.expected_strength: Beats a one-sided margin gate precisely on our failure mode: it suppresses escalations where the 32B would ALSO be wrong (wasted compute) and where the 7B is wrong-but-recoverable. Since ~63% escalation with only 26% saving means many escalations are not worth it, modeling strong-model payoff is the theoretically correct fix, but it requires the 32B-on-calibration labels we currently lack.

methods.name: Gatekeeper confidence-tuning
methods.paper: Gatekeeper: Improving Model Cascades Through Confidence Tuning (2025)
methods.mechanism: Fine-tune the CHEAP model with a hybrid loss: cross-entropy to be confident on its correct answers + KL-to-uniform to be unconfident on its wrong answers. After tuning, deferral uses the same maxprob/entropy threshold, but the confidence is now far better separated between correct and incorrect, so the threshold defers fewer easy items.
methods.signal_required: Cheap-model maxprob/entropy AT INFERENCE (same as margin), but obtained from a confidence-FINE-TUNED cheap model.
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: NO. Requires fine-tuning the 7B weights with the dual loss on labeled data; our 7B is frozen and we do no training. The deployable artifact (router_margin.pkl) is a frozen threshold, incompatible with this method's premise.
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: Full fine-tuning of the 7B with the Gatekeeper loss on PMC-train (correctness labels we DO have), then re-labeling the eval set with the tuned model. Substantial GPU cost.
methods.expected_strength: This is the strongest principled way to beat margin at iso-accuracy: it attacks the root cause (poor correct/incorrect confidence separation) that limits ANY threshold rule, so it can cut escalation rate at fixed accuracy more than any post-hoc signal. But it violates our training-free constraint and needs a 7B fine-tune; include only as the 'if we allow training' upper bound.

methods.name: Post-hoc uncertainty estimators benchmarked for clinical VQA (Label-NLL, sample consistency, semantic entropy)
methods.paper: Uncertainty Is Not a Safety Net for Clinical VQA, but Can It Anticipate Model Failure? (2026)
methods.mechanism: Benchmarks 8 post-hoc, training-free UE signals as failure predictors on clinical VQA: logit-based (avg-NLL, max-NLL, Label-NLL = NLL of the selected answer token), consistency-based (sample consistency across generations, semantic entropy), and embedding-based. Finding: Label-NLL dominates DISCRIMINATION (best at ranking which answers will fail), consistency methods give better CALIBRATION; baseline uncertainty on the unperturbed input predicts which answers will flip under stress.
methods.signal_required: Label-NLL needs the log-prob of the chosen answer token (we have it). Consistency/semantic-entropy need multiple samples. All post-hoc on a deployed VLM.
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: PARTIAL-to-YES for the logit signals. Label-NLL = -logprob of our predicted letter, directly available from the cap320 dict, and avg/max-NLL likewise for single-letter decode. The consistency/semantic-entropy family needs multi-sampling (see ABC/self-consistency rows). The paper's key WARNING applies to us: UE quality collapses on low-accuracy domains like histopathology (~32%), i.e. exactly our PathVQA, so any cheap-confidence gate will be weakest there.
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: NONE for Label-NLL / max-NLL (already in checkpoints). Multi-sample 7B decoding only if we want the consistency-family signals.
methods.expected_strength: Label-NLL is essentially MaxProb on the chosen token and may beat the top1-top2 margin specifically because it scores the SELECTED answer's absolute confidence rather than its lead over the runner-up, which the paper finds is the best single discriminator in clinical VQA. Free to test. The paper also tells us where NOT to expect gains (PathVQA), useful for our per-benchmark 'never worse than 7B' guarantee.

methods.name: Variational VQA risk-averse selective prediction (gBPA)
methods.paper: Variational Visual Question Answering for Uncertainty-Aware Selective Prediction (2025)
methods.mechanism: Variationally fine-tune the VLM (IVON optimizer) to learn a weight posterior; at inference draw MC samples and use a risk-averse selector g_BPA(x) = mean_confidence - std_confidence (a conservative lower-confidence bound ~16th percentile). Abstain/escalate when g_BPA < gamma. Penalizing predictive variance makes selection conservative in high-stakes settings.
methods.signal_required: Multiple MC forward passes (default 64) through sampled weights to get mean and variance of the answer confidence. A deterministic mean-only variant exists but loses the variance signal.
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: NO. Requires variational (IVON) fine-tuning of the 7B to obtain a weight posterior; our 7B is a frozen point estimate. The variance signal cannot be produced from a single deterministic checkpoint.
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: Variational fine-tuning of the 7B plus 64-sample MC inference per question. Heaviest option here.
methods.expected_strength: Wins at the very-low-error-tolerance operating point (their 7-14% gains at <=1% error), which maps to a medical-safety framing; the variance penalty escalates items that are unstable even when mean-confident, catching confidently-wrong cases a margin gate keeps. But it violates training-free and needs 64x inference, so it is only an aspirational comparison, not a near-term gate for our compute-saving objective.

families.family_summary: For training-free VLM/medical-VQA cascades, the SOTA is still a confidence-thresholded Chow rule on the cheap model (MaxProb / Entropy / Margin), with three credible, search-verified ways to do better at iso-accuracy: (1) richer single-pass signals (full-distribution entropy, option-vs-non-option logit gap a la LazyMCoT 2026, free-energy/logsumexp, Label-NLL which clinical-VQA work 2026 finds is the best single failure discriminator); (2) agreement/consistency signals from multiple cheap samples (ABC 2024, self-consistency cascades 2025, AutoMix few-shot self-verification NeurIPS 2024), which beat raw confidence when the cheap model is miscalibrated but unstable; and (3) two-sided / abstention-aware routing (early-abstention cascades 2025, bi-directional proxy confidence 2025) that suppress escalations the strong model would not fix. The hard lesson specific to medical VQA is that cheap-model confidence degrades exactly where accuracy is low (histopathology/PathVQA ~32%), so single-signal gates are structurally weakest there. Given OUR checkpoints, the free wins are entropy/Label-NLL/conformal-threshold swaps and a multi-cap agreement variant (reusing existing cap160/320/640 7B runs); the higher-upside methods (self-consistency, AutoMix self-verify, option-vs-junk gap, raw-logit energy) need only cheap 7B re-runs, while the theoretically-best methods (Gatekeeper confidence-tuning, bi-directional proxy, variational VQA) require either 7B fine-tuning or the 32B-on-calibration labels we deliberately do not have, so they belong as 'if we allow training' upper bounds rather than deployable gates.

methods.name: CP-Router (Conformal Prediction + Full-and-Binary-Entropy routing)
methods.paper: CP-Router: An Uncertainty-Aware Router Between LLM and LRM (AAAI 2026; arXiv 2505.19970)
methods.mechanism: Build a conformal prediction set over the answer options from the cheap LLM's per-option softmax: nonconformity S(x,y)=1-softmax(y), keep options whose score is below the calibrated quantile q-hat. If the set is a singleton (|C(x)|<=1) trust the LLM's top-1; if the set has >1 option, the query is ambiguous -> route to the LRM (reasoning model). FBE (beta*full-entropy + binary-entropy over singleton/non-singleton) adaptively picks the CP error rate alpha to maximize separation of certain vs uncertain inputs.
methods.signal_required: Cheap-model full per-option softmax over the answer letters (A/B/C/D...). No strong-model signal, no sampling, single greedy decode.
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: YES. Our 7B cap320 checkpoints store a full per-letter logprob dict per question, which is exactly the per-option softmax CP-Router needs. The conformal calibration is done on the 7B-on-PMC-train sample using only the 7B's own correctness labels (CP needs gold answers on calibration, which we have), so no 32B labels on calibration are required. The repo already has an FBE/conformal ablation (src/analysis/ablations/gate_alt_conformal*.py, router_conformal_6ds.pkl), so the machinery is in place.
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: NONE. Reuses existing 7B per-letter logprobs and existing PMC-train calibration; only re-derives the threshold/alpha offline.
methods.expected_strength: Beats a single global margin threshold because the decision is set-cardinality (is more than one option still plausible at a coverage-controlled level), not a fixed gap. FBE tunes alpha per the actual confidence distribution, so on benchmarks where the 7B is sharply bimodal (most questions clearly singleton, a minority genuinely ambiguous) it escalates far fewer of the easy-but-modest-margin cases. This is the closest published match to our exact setup (route cheap-LLM -> 32B reasoning LRM on MCQA) and directly targets our problem: 63% escalation at parity suggests our margin threshold is firing on many low-margin-but-correct cases that CP would keep as singletons.

methods.name: Chow rules: Chow-Sum / Chow-Average(perplexity) / Chow-Quantile
methods.paper: Language Model Cascades: Token-level uncertainty and beyond (Gupta et al., ICLR/arXiv 2404.10136)
methods.mechanism: Threshold a scalar confidence derived from the answer token log-probs. Chow-Sum thresholds log p(y|x) (sum of per-token logprobs); Chow-Average thresholds the length-normalized logprob (= negative log-perplexity); Chow-Quantile thresholds a chosen quantile (alpha=0..0.8) of the per-token logprob vector instead of sum/mean. Below threshold -> defer to the large model.
methods.signal_required: Cheap-model per-token logprobs of its greedy answer (for a single-letter answer this collapses to the top-1 letter logprob / the chosen quantile). Single greedy decode, no full softmax strictly required, no strong-model signal.
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: YES for the single-letter case. Our answer is one letter, so Chow-Sum=Chow-Average=the top-1 letter logprob, computable from the per-letter logprob dict. The multi-token Chow-Quantile spread does NOT apply to a one-token answer, so the quantile variant is degenerate for us (this is a limitation, not a blocker). Calibrated on 7B-on-PMC-train with 7B correctness labels.
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: NONE for the single-letter top-1-logprob threshold. To exploit the quantile/per-token-spread variant you would need the 7B to emit a short rationale (multi-token answer) -> a no-think-with-short-CoT GPU re-run.
methods.expected_strength: Max-prob/perplexity thresholding is a slightly different scalar than top1-top2 margin and can win when the absolute confidence (not the gap to second place) better separates correct from wrong - e.g. when the 7B is diffusely uncertain across many options (low max-prob but also low margin) vs confidently-but-narrowly correct (high max-prob, modest margin). On single-letter MCQA the gain over margin is usually small, so this is a cheap sanity baseline rather than a likely big win.

methods.name: Conformal-set deferral via prediction-set cardinality (segregativity for expert choice)
methods.paper: No Need for Learning to Defer? A Training Free Deferral Framework to Multiple Experts through Conformal Prediction (arXiv 2509.12573)
methods.mechanism: Run a split-conformal predictor on the base classifier's softmax (LAC/APS/RAPS scoring). If the prediction set is a singleton, accept the base model's answer; if |set|>1, defer. For multi-expert it then picks the expert by 'segregativity' (which expert best discriminates among the labels remaining in the set). For our 2-model cascade only the singleton-vs-not deferral rule is used.
methods.signal_required: Cheap-model full softmax over the answer options (to build the conformal set). Single forward pass, no sampling, no strong-model signal at inference.
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: PARTIAL/YES. The binary deferral rule (singleton accept, non-singleton escalate) is directly implementable on our 7B per-letter softmax with conformal calibration on PMC-train (calibration needs base-model softmax + gold labels, which we have; per the paper the calibration set needs no expert/strong-model labels). The full multi-expert 'segregativity' selection is irrelevant to a single strong model, so we only borrow the conformal-set deferral half. Heavily overlaps with CP-Router's set rule but without the FBE adaptive-alpha tuning.
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: NONE. Uses existing 7B softmax and existing gold-labeled PMC-train calibration.
methods.expected_strength: Same intuition as CP-Router: cardinality-based deferral with a coverage guarantee escalates only when >=2 options remain statistically plausible, which is a more principled trigger than a hand-set margin and avoids escalating confidently-correct low-margin cases. CP-Router strictly dominates this for our use case (it adds adaptive alpha), so treat this as the static-alpha version / theoretical grounding.

methods.name: C3PO (conformal cost-constrained cascade thresholds)
methods.paper: C3PO: Optimized Large Language Model Cascades with Probabilistic Cost Constraints for Reasoning (arXiv 2511.07396)
methods.mechanism: Each model returns answer + confidence s in [0,1]; exit at the first model where s>=tau_j, else escalate. The thresholds tau_j are chosen NOT against gold labels but by self-supervised agreement with the most-powerful model on an unlabeled split, then validated with conformal prediction to satisfy a probabilistic budget Pr(cost>C*)<=alpha (sort costs, accept tau if the (1-alpha) cost-quantile <= budget).
methods.signal_required: Cheap-model scalar confidence (any calibrated score; max-prob/margin both qualify) PLUS, for the self-supervised threshold-fitting step, the strong model's answers on an unlabeled calibration split (to measure cheap-vs-MPM agreement).
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: PARTIAL. The inference-time gate (confidence>=tau) is trivially implementable on our 7B margin/max-prob. The novelty - fitting tau by agreement with the 32B on a calibration split with the conformal cost guarantee - needs 32B labels on the calibration set, which we do NOT have (calibration is 7B-on-PMC-train only). Our current tau is fit on 7B self-correctness, not 7B-vs-32B agreement, so C3PO's main contribution is exactly the piece we are missing.
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: 32B run on the PMC-train calibration sample (to get strong-model answers for the agreement-based threshold fit). Modest: only the calibration split (~3k), not the eval set.
methods.expected_strength: Wins precisely where our self-correctness calibration is wrong: our tau is set to escalate when the 7B is likely WRONG, but the right criterion for compute saving is to escalate only when the 32B would FLIP the answer to correct. Fitting tau on cheap-vs-strong agreement (plus a hard FLOPs budget via the conformal cost constraint) directly optimizes compute-at-iso-accuracy and gives a formal budget guarantee - the most likely method to push our 63% escalation down without losing parity, at the cost of one 32B calibration run.

methods.name: LogTokU (logits-as-Dirichlet-evidence, decoupled aleatoric/epistemic uncertainty)
methods.paper: Estimating LLM Uncertainty with Evidence / LogTokU (Ma et al., arXiv 2502.00290)
methods.mechanism: Treat the top-K logits at the answer position as Dirichlet evidence (alpha_k). Compute aleatoric uncertainty AU (expected entropy of the Dirichlet) and epistemic uncertainty EU = K / sum(alpha_k+1), then reliability R = 1/(AU*EU). Escalate when reliability is low / EU is high. EU specifically captures 'the model has little evidence here' beyond what softmax probability shows.
methods.signal_required: Cheap-model top-K raw logits (evidence strength), not just normalized probabilities, at the single answer-letter position. Single greedy pass, no sampling, no strong-model signal.
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: PARTIAL. We store per-letter LOGPROBS (post-softmax), not raw pre-softmax logits, and the key claim of LogTokU is that softmax DESTROYS the evidence-strength (total logit mass) that EU needs. AU and the entropy/probability parts are derivable from our logprobs, but the epistemic EU term that is the method's main novelty is not faithfully recoverable from normalized logprobs alone. So we can implement an AU/entropy approximation today but not true EU.
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: Light 7B re-run on the eval+calibration sets that dumps raw top-K logits (or full pre-softmax logits) at the answer position instead of normalized logprobs, to get the evidence magnitude for EU.
methods.expected_strength: Beats margin/max-prob when the 7B is 'confidently wrong by softmax' - cases where probabilities look peaked (large margin, so margin gate keeps them) but the underlying logit evidence is weak (high EU), i.e. genuine knowledge gaps the 32B could fix. Routing on EU should catch exactly the low-margin-look-fine-but-actually-guessing medical questions that a margin threshold lets through, improving accuracy at a given escalation budget. Requires the logit re-run to realize the gain.

methods.name: Direct-answer confidence gating for when-to-reason (CoT-necessity routing)
methods.paper: Can Confidence Estimates Decide When Chain-of-Thought Is Necessary for LLMs? (arXiv 2510.21007)
methods.mechanism: Take the cheap model's DIRECT (no-think) answer confidence; if confidence is high, skip reasoning and accept it, if low, invoke chain-of-thought/the reasoning path. The paper benchmarks which confidence estimate best predicts 'reasoning is needed here' and finds single-pass logit confidence from the direct answer is the practical, training-free choice.
methods.signal_required: Cheap no-think model's answer-token logits/probability (max-prob, margin, or entropy all evaluated). Single forward pass, no sampling.
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: YES (it is essentially a study of exactly our gate). It validates using the 7B no-think per-letter logprobs (max-prob/margin/entropy) to decide whether to spend the 32B's think compute - identical to our pipeline. Directly usable to justify and to pick the best single-pass signal among max-prob/margin/entropy on our existing checkpoints with PMC-train calibration; no new method machinery needed.
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: NONE. Pure offline comparison of max-prob vs margin vs entropy on the 7B logprobs we already have.
methods.expected_strength: Not a new gate so much as guidance on which free signal best decides reasoning-necessity; its value is telling us whether entropy or max-prob (rather than top1-top2 margin) is the stronger trigger for escalating to a THINK model specifically. If entropy over the full option set separates 'needs reasoning' better than the top-2 gap on our med-VQA distribution, swapping the signal could cut escalation at iso-accuracy for zero extra compute.

methods.name: Semantic Agreement cascade (meaning-level consensus deferral)
methods.paper: Semantic Agreement Enables Efficient Open-Ended LLM Cascades (EMNLP 2025 Industry; arXiv 2509.21837)
methods.mechanism: Generate an ENSEMBLE of cheap-model outputs, cluster them by meaning, and use semantic agreement (consensus) as the deferral signal: if the diverse outputs agree semantically, accept the cheap answer; if they disagree, defer to the strong model. Consensus is argued to be a stronger reliability signal than token-level confidence.
methods.signal_required: MULTIPLE cheap-model outputs per query (an ensemble via repeated sampling / varied prompts) - generated text only, no logprobs, works on black-box APIs.
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: NO (not on current checkpoints). We have a SINGLE greedy decode per question with no generated rationale, so there is nothing to cluster - semantic agreement is undefined on a single deterministic letter. It also presumes open-ended outputs; for closed MCQA letters 'semantic agreement' degenerates to answer-vote consistency, which still needs multiple samples we do not have.
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: 7B temperature>0 multi-sample re-run (k samples per question, e.g. k=3-5) over eval+calibration to form the ensemble and measure agreement/vote-consistency.
methods.expected_strength: Wins when single-pass confidence is miscalibrated but resampling reveals instability (the model flips answers across samples) - a complementary signal to logits. On MCQA this reduces to self-consistency vote margin. The downside for our objective is cost: generating k cheap samples multiplies the cheap leg's compute, so it only helps compute-at-iso-accuracy if the avoided 32B calls outweigh k-x the cheap cost; given the 7B is already cheap relative to a 32B think pass, a small k could still net-save, but it needs a GPU re-run to test.

methods.name: AutoMix (few-shot self-verification + POMDP/meta-verifier router)
methods.paper: AutoMix: Automatically Mixing Language Models (Aggarwal, Madaan et al., NeurIPS 2024; arXiv 2310.12963)
methods.mechanism: 3 steps: cheap model answers; cheap model self-verifies its own answer via few-shot in-context prompting (a noisy correctness probe); a POMDP-based meta-verifier maps the (noisy) self-verification probability to a route decision (return cheap answer or escalate to the large model).
