methods.signal_required: Cheap model's self-verification output (a second generation: 'is this answer correct?') - i.e. extra generated text, not its first-answer logits. No strong-model signal at inference.
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: NO on current checkpoints (the self-verification probe is not stored). The POMDP router parameters are fit on a small calibration set without weight training (training-free in that sense), but the core signal - a self-verification pass - was never run. The first-answer logprobs we have are not the AutoMix signal.
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: A second 7B forward pass per question: feed the question+image+its own answer back with a few-shot 'verify this answer' prompt to get the self-verification probability over eval+calibration. (Plus fitting the small POMDP/meta-verifier on PMC-train, which needs 7B-correctness, available.)
methods.expected_strength: Self-verification can catch errors that confidence misses: the model may answer confidently (high margin) yet, when explicitly asked to check, surface a flaw - decoupling 'how peaked is my distribution' from 'do I endorse this answer on reflection'. The POMDP denoises the noisy verifier and can beat a raw threshold by combining the verification signal with prior reliability. For us the cost is one extra cheap verification pass per question; whether it net-saves vs our margin gate depends on how many 32B calls it avoids, and it requires the verification re-run to evaluate.

methods.name: GATEKEEPER (confidence-tuned cascade) -- NOT training-free, included as the SOTA contrast
methods.paper: GATEKEEPER: Improving Model Cascades Through Confidence Tuning (NeurIPS 2025; arXiv 2502.19335)
methods.mechanism: Fine-tune the SMALL model with a confidence-tuning objective so it learns to be confident on questions it gets right and unconfident on ones it should defer; deferral is then a simple threshold on the (now better-calibrated) small-model confidence.
methods.signal_required: Same inference signal as a plain threshold (small-model confidence), but obtained from a FINE-TUNED small model.
methods.implementable_on_our_ckpts: NO as a training-free method - it requires gradient fine-tuning of the 7B, which violates our training-free constraint and is not supported by our frozen checkpoints. Listed only as the current learned-gate SOTA to benchmark our training-free gate against and to bound how much headroom a training-based approach claims over a raw threshold.
methods.needs_gpu_rerun: Full supervised fine-tuning of the 7B with the confidence-tuning loss (out of scope for training-free).
methods.expected_strength: It beats a plain confidence threshold by construction because it reshapes the confidence distribution to be deferral-aware rather than thresholding an off-the-shelf, miscalibrated confidence. Relevant to us as the ceiling: it quantifies how much of the gap between our margin gate and an oracle is attributable to 7B miscalibration (which the training-free conformal/agreement-based methods above try to recover without fine-tuning).

families.family_summary: The 2025-2026 training-free cascade literature has converged on a clear message that is directly relevant to our 7B(no-think)->32B(reasoning) med-VQA setup: a single global top1-top2 margin threshold is a weak gate, and the strongest training-free improvements come from (a) conformal-prediction set-cardinality routing and (b) calibrating the threshold against cheap-vs-strong AGREEMENT rather than cheap-model self-correctness. CP-Router (AAAI 2026, arXiv 2505.19970) is the closest match to our exact problem - it routes MCQA from a cheap LLM to a reasoning LRM using a conformal set over the answer-option softmax plus a Full-and-Binary-Entropy criterion to adaptively pick the coverage level, is fully training-free, and is implementable on our existing 7B per-letter logprob dicts with no GPU re-run; it (and the related conformal-set deferral of arXiv 2509.12573, plus our repo's existing FBE ablation) is the highest-priority thing to try. C3PO (arXiv 2511.07396) targets exactly our suspected weakness - our tau is fit on 7B self-correctness, but compute-at-iso-accuracy is really optimized by deferring only when the 32B would flip the answer; C3PO fits thresholds on cheap-vs-strong agreement under a conformal FLOPs budget, requiring just one 32B run on our ~3k calibration split. Single-pass evidential and confidence signals (LogTokU's logit-as-Dirichlet epistemic uncertainty, the Chow max-prob/perplexity rules, and the CoT-necessity confidence study) are cheap to try but mostly need either raw logits (a light 7B logit-dump re-run) or are near-degenerate on single-letter answers, while sampling/verification-based methods (Semantic Agreement, AutoMix) need genuine GPU re-runs (multi-sample or self-verification passes) and are less certain to net-save given the 7B is already cheap. The recurring caveat across the family is that learned gates (e.g. GATEKEEPER) still claim headroom over any training-free gate by fine-tuning the small model's calibration - so for a strictly training-free win our best bets are conformal/FBE routing on existing logprobs (zero re-run) and agreement-calibrated thresholds (one cheap 32B calibration run).

ranked_implementable.name: Predictive entropy of the 7B per-letter distribution (single-pass option entropy)
ranked_implementable.rank_reason: Empirically the best-discriminating single-pass score on our own data: AUC for flagging 7B errors on the 4 competent benchmarks = 0.6856, beating Gini (0.6817), max-prob (0.6775), and the deployed margin (0.6668). Uses the WHOLE distribution, so it catches 3-4-way diffuse confusions that margin's top1-top2 gap misses (verified: our dicts hold 8.2 letters on avg and effectively renormalize to ~1.0). Zero re-run, zero training, calibration-only.
ranked_implementable.how_to_implement_on_ckpts: For each row, softmax opt_logprobs over its letters (they already sum to ~1.0; renormalize for safety), compute H=-sum p_i log p_i. Escalate when H > tau_H. Calibrate tau_H on ckpts/gate_7b_pmctrain_prune/cap320/ckpt_nothink.jsonl: pick the smallest tau_H whose 7B-kept error rate (on the rows with H<=tau_H, using the row's own 'ok') equals the 7B's overall PMC-train error minus the target margin, or just sweep tau_H to the escalation budget that matched the deployed gate. Report frontier-matched vs the deployed margin gate, exactly as src/analysis/ablations/gate_ablation_bakeoff.py already does for entropy (extend it to be the headline, not a footnote).
ranked_implementable.signal: AUC 0.686 (vs margin 0.667) for 7B-error discrimination on competent-4; strictly richer scalar than margin at zero cost.

ranked_implementable.name: Gini impurity / DOCTOR D_alpha (TBB variant)
ranked_implementable.rank_reason: Second-best single-pass discriminator on our data (AUC 0.6817 > margin 0.6668), a different operating curve than entropy (weights the head of the distribution more), so it can win at a different budget. Fully training-free, computable today from opt_logprobs, no 32B labels needed.
ranked_implementable.how_to_implement_on_ckpts: Per row: softmax opt_logprobs, compute g=sum_k p_k^2, Gini=1-g; escalate when Gini>gamma (equivalently DOCTOR D_alpha: escalate when (1-g)>alpha*g). Calibrate gamma on PMC-train cap320 with the 7B's own 'ok' the same way as entropy/margin. Add as a column in gate_ablation_bakeoff.py.
ranked_implementable.signal: AUC 0.682 vs margin 0.667; distinct curve from entropy.

ranked_implementable.name: Conformal prediction-set-size deferral / CP-Router (LAC/APS/RAPS, FBE alpha-selection)
ranked_implementable.rank_reason: Best-fit conformal method: uses exactly our signal (7B per-letter softmax) and exactly our calibration (7B own correctness on PMC-train, no 32B labels). Escalating non-singleton sets is scale-free across the 6 heterogeneous benchmarks, which directly addresses the cross-benchmark transfer weakness of a single raw-margin tau. Our repo already has a faithful conformal/FBE implementation (src/analysis/ablations/gate_alt_conformal*.py and PART B of gate_ablation_bakeoff.py), so this is low-effort to finalize and report.
ranked_implementable.how_to_implement_on_ckpts: LAC nonconformity score s(x,y)=1-p(y); compute calibration quantile qhat at level alpha from PMC-train cap320 rows (using gold letter as y_true). At eval, build C(x)={y: 1-p(y) <= qhat}; escalate iff |C(x)|>1 (non-singleton). Sweep alpha; pick alpha* by FBE (maximize separation of set-size distributions, beta~3) as in the existing script. Also try APS/RAPS scores for more singletons on heavy-tailed dicts. Compare frontier-matched to margin.
ranked_implementable.signal: Calibrated, benchmark-invariant set-size cut; existing partial implementation shows it is Pareto-competitive with margin.

ranked_implementable.name: Conformal Risk Control (CRC) / Learn-then-Test (LTT) threshold selection wrapping our best score
ranked_implementable.rank_reason: Not a new signal but the principled replacement for the hand-frozen tau=0.426. Turns 'pick tau' into 'pick the least-escalation threshold whose 7B-kept error is provably <= alpha (CRC: in expectation; LTT: w.p. 1-delta)'. Our deployed tau is likely conservative, so the certified threshold can lower escalation at the same accuracy floor. Pure post-hoc, no re-run, only needs 7B own-correctness on PMC-train (which we have, n=3000).
ranked_implementable.how_to_implement_on_ckpts: Choose the score (entropy/Gini/set-size). Define loss = 7B error on kept inputs as a monotone function of threshold lambda. CRC: smallest lambda s.t. (n*Rhat(lambda)+B)/(n+1) <= alpha on PMC-train (B=loss bound=1). LTT: order a lambda grid, compute Bentkus/Hoeffding p-values for H_lambda: risk(lambda)<=alpha on PMC-train, apply fixed-sequence testing, take the least-escalation lambda that passes at delta. Then evaluate that lambda on the 6 benchmarks.
ranked_implementable.signal: Certified operating point; lets you state a finite-sample guarantee on kept-set error, a publishable rigor upgrade over a heuristic tau.

ranked_implementable.name: Temperature-scaled confidence before thresholding
ranked_implementable.rank_reason: Cheap calibration-only upgrade that improves CROSS-BENCHMARK transfer of a single threshold (our six benchmarks differ in difficulty; one raw tau over- or under-escalates). T is a monotone transform so it cannot change within-set sample ranking, but it re-places where the threshold sits and is documented to help when the 7B is miscalibrated (likely for a small med VLM). Already scaffolded (fit_T in gate_ablation_bakeoff.py).
ranked_implementable.how_to_implement_on_ckpts: Fit one scalar T on PMC-train cap320 by minimizing NLL of the gold letter under softmax(logprobs/T) (grid 0.3..5.0). Rescale eval logprobs by 1/T, renormalize, then apply margin/maxprob/entropy threshold. Report whether the SAME calibrated tau transfers across benchmarks better than the raw tau (compare per-benchmark escalation/accuracy).
ranked_implementable.signal: Targets the transfer/over-escalation problem directly; modest within-set gain but better single-threshold generalization.

ranked_implementable.name: Max-probability / Chow's rule baseline (and Chow-Average, which degenerates to it)
ranked_implementable.rank_reason: Canonical Bayes reject-option baseline every cascade paper reports; on our data it already edges margin (AUC 0.6775 vs 0.6668). Must be in the bake-off as the reference point even though it is unlikely to be the headline winner. Chow-Sum/Chow-Average collapse to this for our single-letter decode.
ranked_implementable.how_to_implement_on_ckpts: Per row: maxprob = exp(max logprob) after renormalization; escalate when maxprob<t. Calibrate t on PMC-train cap320 via 7B own-correctness, same protocol as margin. Note Chow-Average = chosen-letter prob = maxprob here (gen_tokens=2, single answer token), so report them as one entry.
ranked_implementable.signal: AUC 0.678; standard reference, near-monotone with entropy/margin in MCQ.

ranked_implementable.name: Cross-cap agreement ensemble (cap80/160/320/640 prediction disagreement)
ranked_implementable.rank_reason: Zero-re-run agreement signal unique to our setup: we already have the 7B decoded at four resolution caps, forming a ready-made cheap ensemble. Alone it is weak (AUC 0.566, caps agree ~92% of the time) but it is partially INDEPENDENT of the logprob-shape signals, so it is most valuable as an extra feature combined with entropy/margin (escalate if entropy high OR caps disagree), not as a standalone gate.
ranked_implementable.how_to_implement_on_ckpts: For each eval idx, gather pred from ckpts/gate_7b_prune/{cap80,cap160,cap320,cap640}/ckpt_{ds}_nothink_norag.jsonl; signal = fraction of caps disagreeing with the cap320 pred (or count of distinct preds). Calibrate the combine threshold on the matching PMC-train caps (note: only cap320 PMC-train exists today; for a clean held-out combine you'd need PMC-train at the other caps, otherwise calibrate the combine weights on a held-out eval split and report as analysis). Use as a tie-breaker on low-margin cases.
ranked_implementable.signal: AUC 0.566 standalone but decorrelated from logprob signals; combine-only value.

needs_gpu.name: Recoverability-aware post-hoc deferral (Jitkrittum et al. NeurIPS 2023 / Hybrid-LLM gap-router / post-hoc L2D)
needs_gpu.gpu_run_needed: Run the 32B (think mode, predicted LETTER only — no logprobs needed) on the held-out PMC-VQA train calibration split (the same ~3000 idxs in ckpts/gate_7b_pmctrain_prune/cap320). This gives (7B-signals, 7B-correct, 32B-correct) triples on calibration, which we currently lack.
needs_gpu.why_worth_it: This is the single highest-leverage run. Our own data shows 58.4% of 7B-wrong cases are FUTILE to escalate (32B also wrong) and 21.6% of 7B-correct cases would be FLIPPED WRONG by the 32B. Margin escalates blindly on 7B uncertainty, wasting compute on the futile mass — exactly why it escalates 63% but saves only 26%. A rule trained to predict net escalation BENEFIT z=1[32B-right AND 7B-wrong] (a tiny logistic/GBM on the 7B logprob features) would stop escalating unrecoverable and harmful cases. The futile-aware oracle floor on our data is ~2.3% escalation for parity vs margin's 29.4% oracle — enormous headroom.

needs_gpu.name: Self-consistency / sampled-answer agreement (Mixture-of-Thoughts cascade)
needs_gpu.gpu_run_needed: Re-run the 7B at cap320 with temperature sampling, k=5-10 stochastic decodes per question, on eval + PMC-train; signal = majority-vote agreement fraction.
needs_gpu.why_worth_it: Med-VQA UQ studies report sample-consistency has the best error-discrimination among cheap proxies; it captures epistemic uncertainty a single greedy logprob misses. BUT the k-fold cheap-leg cost directly eats the FLOPs saving, so it only wins if it cuts escalation far more than the extra k passes cost — must be netted in prefill-inclusive FLOPs. Medium priority: strong signal, but the cost accounting is adversarial to our objective and our single-pass entropy already approximates the k->inf limit for MCQ.

needs_gpu.name: P(True) self-evaluation (Kadavath et al.) / AutoMix-threshold self-verification
needs_gpu.gpu_run_needed: One extra short 7B greedy forward pass per question: re-prompt with the chosen answer ('Is this answer correct given the image? yes/no') and read P(yes). On eval + PMC-train. No 32B labels needed.
needs_gpu.why_worth_it: A second introspective pass can decorrelate errors from the first-pass letter distribution and catch confident-but-wrong cases that margin/entropy pass through. Only ~1 extra short pass (much cheaper than k-sample consistency). Worth a pilot, but med-VLM self-verification may be as miscalibrated as the answer softmax; uncertain upside.

needs_gpu.name: True Max-Logit (unnormalized) over answer tokens
needs_gpu.gpu_run_needed: Cheap 7B cap320 re-run dumping RAW pre-softmax answer-token logits (greedy, 1 token, same passes we already do — just save logits instead of log-softmax).
needs_gpu.why_worth_it: Plaut et al. report max-logit correlates with MC correctness at r=0.95 vs MSP r=0.68; our saved log-softmax destroys the cross-question logit magnitude. Low cost to capture, plausible to beat MSP/margin if absolute evidence scale is informative — but the catalog notes gains are usually small in 4-5-way MCQ, so it is a cheap A/B, not a primary bet.

not_applicable: Chow-Quantile / token-level uncertainty (LM Cascades 2024): our 7B cheap leg decodes a SINGLE answer letter (gen_tokens=2), so there is no multi-token sequence to take per-position quantiles over; the length-bias problem it solves does not arise.
TokenSAR / SentSAR / SAR (Duan et al.): require multi-token free-form generations (relevance reweighting is vacuous on one letter) and an auxiliary similarity encoder.

Semantic Entropy / Discrete SE (Kuhn, Farquhar): for single-letter MCQ, meaning-clusters = letters, so SE degenerates to sampled letter-frequency entropy — our analytic option-entropy is the exact K->inf limit at zero cost; the K-sample version needs sampling we don't have.
Verbalized confidence (Tian et al.): needs the 7B to decode a confidence number; not on disk, and small med VLMs are documented to verbalize overconfidently — weakest fit.

Semantic Entropy Probes (Kossen et al.): needs trained hidden-state probes + K-sample SE labels; we never saved cap320 hidden states, and our luck-floor audit (-29 sigma) is direct local evidence that one 7B's internal signal is not routable.

Energy score / MaxLogit from saved data: our stored values are normalized log-softmax (verified: exp-sum ~1.0), so logsumexp ~= 0 and max-logit collapses to log(maxprob)=MSP up to a monotone transform — not recoverable without raw logits (moved to needs_gpu).
Cascade-Aware Training (CAT) and GATEKEEPER: require fine-tuning the 7B with a cascade-aware/confidence-tuning loss — violates training-free and changes the frozen checkpoint.
FrugalGPT DistilBERT scorer: requires training a text-quality scorer on labeled data; not training-free, and adds little over logprobs for single-letter MCQ.

RouteLLM / Hybrid-LLM / kNN-router (query-only routers): decide before the cheap model runs from query text alone, ignoring our richest asset (7B per-letter logprobs), and need pairwise-preference or per-query 32B-gap labels we lack on calibration.

Edge-Cloud Conformal Alignment (CAb): needs the strong model's output DISTRIBUTION on calibration to define conditional-coverage alignment; our 32B is a reasoning model with empty logprobs — no distribution to align to.
Post-Hoc-Embed deferral classifier (LM Cascades): needs strong-model hidden states; our 32B emits neither logprobs nor saved hidden states.
Trust-or-Escalate Simulated Annotators (core signal): needs N few-shot persona passes per question; only its risk-controlled thresholding (= LTT) is portable without a re-run.

novelty_opportunities.idea: Calibration-only recoverability prior via 32B aggregate competence, NOT per-sample 32B labels. Estimate, on the PMC-train calibration set partitioned by a 7B-derived difficulty bin (entropy decile x benchmark), the EMPIRICAL escalation-benefit prior P(32B fixes | 7B wrong, bin) using ONLY the one-time 32B-on-PMC-train letter pass, then deploy a gate that escalates a 7B-uncertain sample only when its bin's recoverability prior exceeds a cost-justified threshold. This is a coarse, transferable surrogate for the per-sample post-hoc deferral rule that needs no per-sample strong-model confidence.
novelty_opportunities.why_novel: Existing recoverability-aware deferral (Jitkrittum, Hybrid-LLM) fits a per-sample classifier requiring dense strong-model labels and assumes the strong model exposes confidence. Ours uses ONLY aggregate strong-model competence binned by cheap-model uncertainty + benchmark, turning recoverability into a low-dimensional calibrated prior that transfers — designed precisely for a logprob-free reasoning strong model.
novelty_opportunities.why_it_could_win: Our data shows 58.4% of escalations are futile and 21.6% are harmful; a bin-level recoverability prior captures most of the futile mass (e.g. near-chance MedXpert bins) at a fraction of the labeling cost, and the futile-aware oracle floor (~2.3% escalation for parity) shows the headroom is enormous. Publishable as 'recoverability-aware cascade deferral without strong-model confidence.'

novelty_opportunities.idea: Distribution-SHAPE gate: a calibrated 2-3 feature score combining entropy + Gini + top1-prob (full-shape) rather than the single top1-top2 margin, fit ONLY on the cheap model's own correctness, with a CRC/LTT-certified threshold. Add the cross-cap disagreement (cap80/160/320/640, already on disk) as a decorrelated 4th feature.
novelty_opportunities.why_novel: Prior work treats these as competing single scalars in a bake-off; we combine the full SHAPE of the answer distribution plus a free resolution-ensemble agreement signal into one calibrated, risk-controlled gate trained only on cheap-model labels — no strong-model labels, no extra inference. The cross-resolution ensemble is unique to a compute-budget cascade and has never been used as an escalation signal.
novelty_opportunities.why_it_could_win: Entropy already beats margin (AUC 0.686 vs 0.667) and Gini/cross-cap are partially independent, so a tiny calibrated combine should push the error-discrimination frontier further; LTT certification gives a publishable finite-sample guarantee and a less-conservative operating point than tau=0.426. Entirely zero-re-run.

novelty_opportunities.idea: Cost-controlled conformal deferral (C3PO-style) that controls the COMPUTE budget rather than accuracy. Use the token_cache.json prefill-inclusive FLOPs as a per-query cost, and pick the conformal-set-size / entropy threshold so that P(test FLOPs > budget) <= alpha, then squeeze maximum accuracy under that budget.
novelty_opportunities.why_novel: Flips the control target from accuracy (CRC on error) to a probabilistic compute-budget guarantee, instantiated with our real measured prefill-inclusive FLOPs and a logprob-free strong model — the cost-control conformal cascade has not been demonstrated on a medical VLM with honest FLOPs accounting.
novelty_opportunities.why_it_could_win: Our stated objective IS to maximize compute saving at parity; a method that provably pins 'never exceed X% of always-32B FLOPs w.p. 1-alpha' and reports the accuracy achieved is exactly the paper's deliverable framed as a guarantee, and is a cleaner contribution than a hand-tuned operating point.

novelty_opportunities.idea: Futile-escalation short-circuit on the cheap leg (early-abstention adapted to forced-choice). When the 7B-uncertainty is high AND the bin-level recoverability prior is low (32B also expected to fail), KEEP the 7B answer instead of escalating — converting 'abstain' into 'don't waste the 32B call' for our must-answer MCQ setting.
novelty_opportunities.why_novel: Early-abstention cascades drop queries; in forced-choice med-VQA you must answer, so we reinterpret the abstain branch as 'retain cheap answer on unrecoverable cases.' This targeted short-circuit of the futile set, gated by a transferable recoverability prior, is a new framing for must-answer cascades.
novelty_opportunities.why_it_could_win: 58.4% of escalations buy nothing; short-circuiting even half of them at iso-accuracy roughly halves the 32B call rate, directly attacking the 'escalate 63%, save 26%' pathology — the largest single lever in our results.

novelty_opportunities.idea: Selective-disagreement gate: escalate ONLY where the 7B's answer distribution is BOTH uncertain (high entropy) AND its top-1 is unstable across resolution caps. Treats the two as an AND-gate so confidently-stable answers are never escalated regardless of absolute entropy.
novelty_opportunities.why_novel: Combines intrinsic (distribution-shape) and extrinsic (resolution-perturbation) uncertainty into a conjunctive rule, using the existing multi-cap checkpoints as a free perturbation ensemble — a perturbation-stability escalation criterion specific to resolution-budget VLM cascades.
novelty_opportunities.why_it_could_win: The two signals are decorrelated (entropy AUC 0.686, cross-cap AUC 0.566), so an AND-gate can suppress escalation on the large mass of high-entropy-but-stable easy-benchmark items that margin/entropy over-escalate, cutting escalation below the single-signal frontier at parity. Zero re-run.

synthesis.overall_assessment: Strongest baselines to beat: the incumbent margin gate is NOT the strongest single-pass score on our own data — entropy (error-discrimination AUC 0.686), Gini (0.682), and even max-prob (0.678) all beat margin (0.667) on the 4 competent benchmarks, and conformal set-size (CP-Router/FBE) plus a CRC/LTT-certified threshold are the principled calibration-only upgrades that are immediately implementable with NO GPU re-run and NO 32B labels (only the 3000-row PMC-train cap320 set with 7B own-correctness, which we have). These should be finalized in the existing src/analysis/ablations/gate_ablation_bakeoff.py as frontier-matched comparisons; entropy/Gini/conformal are the realistic offline wins. The single most promising direction for a novel SOTA method is RECOVERABILITY-AWARE deferral: our checkpoints prove that 58.4% of escalations are futile (32B also wrong) and 21.6% of 7B-correct answers would be flipped wrong by the 32B, which is exactly why margin escalates 63% but saves only 26% — and the futile-aware oracle floor is ~2.3% escalation for parity (vs margin's 29.4% oracle), an enormous headroom. The publishable novelty is to capture this without per-sample strong-model confidence (the 32B is logprob-free): build a calibrated, transferable BIN-LEVEL recoverability prior P(32B fixes | 7B-uncertainty-bin x benchmark) from a single cheap 32B-on-PMC-train LETTER-only pass, and gate escalation on (cheap-model uncertainty) AND (bin recoverability high enough to justify the FLOPs), optionally framed as a cost-controlled conformal guarantee on prefill-inclusive FLOPs. That one extra run — 32B predicted letters on the existing PMC-train calibration idxs — is the highest-leverage GPU investment in this project and unlocks both the SOTA method and a clean efficiency-with-guarantee paper for CVGIP 2026."
